  <script>
    document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(btn => {
      btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
        document.querySelectorAll('.tab-content').forEach(c => c.classList.remove('active'));
        btn.classList.add('active');
        document.getElementById(btn.getAttribute('data-tab')).classList.add('active');
        if (btn.getAttribute('data-tab') === 'tab-logs') refreshLogs();
      });
    });

    async function refreshStatus() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/status');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        document.getElementById('kpi-map').textContent = (d.map || 'PRISONER').toUpperCase();
        document.getElementById('kpi-mode').textContent = `MODO: ${(d.variant || d.gametype || 'SLAYER').toUpperCase()}`;
        document.getElementById('kpi-players').textContent = `${d.players || 0} / ${d.max_players || 128}`;
        document.getElementById('kpi-tick').textContent = `${(d.tickrate || 30.0).toFixed(1)} HZ`;
        document.getElementById('table-count').textContent = `${d.players || 0} PRESENTES`;
        
        // Memoria y Uptime reales
        if (d.rss_kb) {
          const mb = (d.rss_kb / 1024).toFixed(1);
          document.getElementById('kpi-ram').textContent = `${mb} MB`;
        }
        if (d.uptime) {
          const hrs = Math.floor(d.uptime / 3600);
          const mins = Math.floor((d.uptime % 3600) / 60);
          document.getElementById('kpi-uptime').textContent = `UPTIME: ${hrs}h ${mins}m`;
        }
        if (d.node_info) {
          document.getElementById('node-env-tag').textContent = `NODE: ${d.node_info} · NETCODE: V${d.network_version || 39}`;
        }
        if (d.name) {
          document.getElementById('host-badge').textContent = `HOST: ${d.name}`;
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function refreshPlayers() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/players');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        const tbody = document.getElementById('players-body');
        if (!d.players || d.players.length === 0) {
          tbody.innerHTML = '<tr><td colspan="6" style="text-align:center;color:var(--text-muted);padding:24px;">NO HAY JUGADORES HUMANOS CONECTADOS.</td></tr>';
          return;
        }
        tbody.innerHTML = d.players.map(p => `
          <tr>
            <td>[${p.slot}]</td>
            <td><strong>${p.name}</strong></td>
            <td>${p.team === 0 ? 'ROJO' : 'AZUL'}</td>
            <td>${p.score || 0}</td>
            <td>${p.ping || 0} ms</td>
            <td style="text-align:right;">
              <button class="hud-btn" style="padding:2px 8px;font-size:12px;" onclick="execHs('kick ${p.name}')">KICK</button>
              <button class="hud-btn hud-btn-red" style="padding:2px 8px;font-size:12px;" onclick="execHs('ban ${p.name}')">BAN</button>
            </td>
          </tr>
        `).join('');
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function refreshLogs() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/log');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        const out = document.getElementById('logs-output');
        if (d.lines && d.lines.length > 0) {
          out.textContent = d.lines.join('\n');
          out.scrollTop = out.scrollHeight;
        } else {
          out.textContent = 'NO HAY ENTRADAS DE LOG DISPONIBLES EN DEBUG.TXT';
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function loadSettings() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/settings');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        if (d.settings) {
          d.settings.forEach(s => {
            if (s.name === 'network.server_name') document.getElementById('cfg-name').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'debug.network_test_countdown') document.getElementById('cfg-countdown').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'debug.network_test_time') document.getElementById('cfg-time').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'server.region') {
              document.getElementById('cfg-region').value = s.value;
              document.getElementById('region-badge').textContent = `ONLINE · ${s.value.toUpperCase()}`;
            }
            if (s.name === 'server.chat_filter') document.getElementById('cfg-filter').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'network.map_rotation') document.getElementById('cfg-rot-mode').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'network.afk_timeout') document.getElementById('cfg-afk').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'webhooks.discord') document.getElementById('cfg-discord').value = s.value || '';
            if (s.name === 'webhooks.telegram') document.getElementById('cfg-telegram').value = s.value || '';
          });
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function saveSettings() {
      const payload = {
        "network.server_name": document.getElementById('cfg-name').value,
        "debug.network_test_countdown": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-countdown').value) || 1,
        "debug.network_test_time": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-time').value) || 15,
        "server.region": document.getElementById('cfg-region').value,
        "server.chat_filter": document.getElementById('cfg-filter').value,
        "network.map_rotation": document.getElementById('cfg-rot-mode').value,
        "network.afk_timeout": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-afk').value) || 180,
        "webhooks.discord": document.getElementById('cfg-discord').value,
        "webhooks.telegram": document.getElementById('cfg-telegram').value
      };
      try {
        await fetch('/api/settings', {
          method: 'PUT',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify(payload)
        });
        showToast('PARAMETROS APLICADOS EN CALIENTE');
        refreshStatus();
      } catch (e) {
        showToast('ERROR AL APLICAR');
      }
    }

    async function execHs(cmd) {
      try {
        await fetch('/api/command', {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ line: cmd })
        });
        showToast('COMANDO EJECUTADO: ' + cmd);
        logCli('> ' + cmd + ' [OK]');
      } catch (e) {
        showToast('ERROR AL EJECUTAR');
      }
    }

    function execPlayer(action) {
      const name = document.getElementById('mod-target').value.trim();
      if (!name) return;
      execHs(action + ' ' + name);
      document.getElementById('mod-target').value = '';
    }

    function sendCli() {
      const inp = document.getElementById('cli-input');
      const val = inp.value.trim();
      if (!val) return;
      execHs(val);
      inp.value = '';
    }

    function logCli(text) {
      const out = document.getElementById('cli-output');
      out.textContent += '\n' + text;
      out.scrollTop = out.scrollHeight;
    }

    function showToast(text) {
      const t = document.getElementById('hud-toast');
      t.textContent = text;
      t.style.display = 'block';
      setTimeout(() => { t.style.display = 'none'; }, 2500);
    }

    document.getElementById('btn-save-ops').addEventListener('click', saveSettings);
    document.getElementById('btn-save-full').addEventListener('click', saveSettings);
    document.getElementById('btn-skip').addEventListener('click', async () => {
      await fetch('/api/rotation/play', { method: 'POST' });
      showToast('SALTANDO A SIGUIENTE PARTIDA...');
      setTimeout(refreshStatus, 1500);
    });
    document.getElementById('btn-shuffle').addEventListener('click', () => execHs('sv_map beavercreek slayer'));
    document.getElementById('btn-stop').addEventListener('click', () => execHs('sv_end_game'));

    setInterval(refreshStatus, 3000);
    setInterval(refreshPlayers, 3000);
    refreshStatus();
    refreshPlayers();
    loadSettings();
  </script>
</body>
</html>

```

  <script>
    document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(btn => {
      btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
        document.querySelectorAll('.tab-content').forEach(c => c.classList.remove('active'));
        btn.classList.add('active');
        document.getElementById(btn.getAttribute('data-tab')).classList.add('active');
        if (btn.getAttribute('data-tab') === 'tab-logs') refreshLogs();
      });
    });

    async function refreshStatus() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/status');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        document.getElementById('kpi-map').textContent = (d.map || 'PRISONER').toUpperCase();
        document.getElementById('kpi-mode').textContent = `MODO: ${(d.variant || d.gametype || 'SLAYER').toUpperCase()}`;
        document.getElementById('kpi-players').textContent = `${d.players || 0} / ${d.max_players || 128}`;
        document.getElementById('kpi-tick').textContent = `${(d.tickrate || 30.0).toFixed(1)} HZ`;
        document.getElementById('table-count').textContent = `${d.players || 0} PRESENTES`;
        
        // Memoria y Uptime reales
        if (d.rss_kb) {
          const mb = (d.rss_kb / 1024).toFixed(1);
          document.getElementById('kpi-ram').textContent = `${mb} MB`;
        }
        if (d.uptime) {
          const hrs = Math.floor(d.uptime / 3600);
          const mins = Math.floor((d.uptime % 3600) / 60);
          document.getElementById('kpi-uptime').textContent = `UPTIME: ${hrs}h ${mins}m`;
        }
        if (d.node_info) {
          document.getElementById('node-env-tag').textContent = `NODE: ${d.node_info} · NETCODE: V${d.network_version || 39}`;
        }
        if (d.name) {
          document.getElementById('host-badge').textContent = `HOST: ${d.name}`;
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function refreshPlayers() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/players');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        const tbody = document.getElementById('players-body');
        if (!d.players || d.players.length === 0) {
          tbody.innerHTML = '<tr><td colspan="6" style="text-align:center;color:var(--text-muted);padding:24px;">NO HAY JUGADORES HUMANOS CONECTADOS.</td></tr>';
          return;
        }
        tbody.innerHTML = d.players.map(p => `
          <tr>
            <td>[${p.slot}]</td>
            <td><strong>${p.name}</strong></td>
            <td>${p.team === 0 ? 'ROJO' : 'AZUL'}</td>
            <td>${p.score || 0}</td>
            <td>${p.ping || 0} ms</td>
            <td style="text-align:right;">
              <button class="hud-btn" style="padding:2px 8px;font-size:12px;" onclick="execHs('kick ${p.name}')">KICK</button>
              <button class="hud-btn hud-btn-red" style="padding:2px 8px;font-size:12px;" onclick="execHs('ban ${p.name}')">BAN</button>
            </td>
          </tr>
        `).join('');
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function refreshLogs() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/log');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        const out = document.getElementById('logs-output');
        if (d.lines && d.lines.length > 0) {
          out.textContent = d.lines.join('\n');
          out.scrollTop = out.scrollHeight;
        } else {
          out.textContent = 'NO HAY ENTRADAS DE LOG DISPONIBLES EN DEBUG.TXT';
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function loadSettings() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/settings');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        if (d.settings) {
          d.settings.forEach(s => {
            if (s.name === 'network.server_name') document.getElementById('cfg-name').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'debug.network_test_countdown') document.getElementById('cfg-countdown').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'debug.network_test_time') document.getElementById('cfg-time').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'server.region') {
              document.getElementById('cfg-region').value = s.value;
              document.getElementById('region-badge').textContent = `ONLINE · ${s.value.toUpperCase()}`;
            }
            if (s.name === 'server.chat_filter') document.getElementById('cfg-filter').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'network.map_rotation') document.getElementById('cfg-rot-mode').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'network.afk_timeout') document.getElementById('cfg-afk').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'webhooks.discord') document.getElementById('cfg-discord').value = s.value || '';
            if (s.name === 'webhooks.telegram') document.getElementById('cfg-telegram').value = s.value || '';
          });
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function saveSettings() {
      const payload = {
        "network.server_name": document.getElementById('cfg-name').value,
        "debug.network_test_countdown": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-countdown').value) || 1,
        "debug.network_test_time": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-time').value) || 15,
        "server.region": document.getElementById('cfg-region').value,
        "server.chat_filter": document.getElementById('cfg-filter').value,
        "network.map_rotation": document.getElementById('cfg-rot-mode').value,
        "network.afk_timeout": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-afk').value) || 180,
        "webhooks.discord": document.getElementById('cfg-discord').value,
        "webhooks.telegram": document.getElementById('cfg-telegram').value
      };
      try {
        await fetch('/api/settings', {
          method: 'PUT',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify(payload)
        });
        showToast('PARAMETROS APLICADOS EN CALIENTE');
        refreshStatus();
      } catch (e) {
        showToast('ERROR AL APLICAR');
      }
    }

    async function execHs(cmd) {
      try {
        await fetch('/api/command', {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ line: cmd })
        });
        showToast('COMANDO EJECUTADO: ' + cmd);
        logCli('> ' + cmd + ' [OK]');
      } catch (e) {
        showToast('ERROR AL EJECUTAR');
      }
    }

    function execPlayer(action) {
      const name = document.getElementById('mod-target').value.trim();
      if (!name) return;
      execHs(action + ' ' + name);
      document.getElementById('mod-target').value = '';
    }

    function sendCli() {
      const inp = document.getElementById('cli-input');
      const val = inp.value.trim();
      if (!val) return;
      execHs(val);
      inp.value = '';
    }

    function logCli(text) {
      const out = document.getElementById('cli-output');
      out.textContent += '\n' + text;
      out.scrollTop = out.scrollHeight;
    }

    function showToast(text) {
      const t = document.getElementById('hud-toast');
      t.textContent = text;
      t.style.display = 'block';
      setTimeout(() => { t.style.display = 'none'; }, 2500);
    }

    document.getElementById('btn-save-ops').addEventListener('click', saveSettings);
    document.getElementById('btn-save-full').addEventListener('click', saveSettings);
    document.getElementById('btn-skip').addEventListener('click', async () => {
      await fetch('/api/rotation/play', { method: 'POST' });
      showToast('SALTANDO A SIGUIENTE PARTIDA...');
      setTimeout(refreshStatus, 1500);
    });
    document.getElementById('btn-shuffle').addEventListener('click', () => execHs('sv_map beavercreek slayer'));
    document.getElementById('btn-stop').addEventListener('click', () => execHs('sv_end_game'));

    setInterval(refreshStatus, 3000);
    setInterval(refreshPlayers, 3000);
    refreshStatus();
    refreshPlayers();
    loadSettings();
  </script>
</body>
</html>

```

  <script>
    document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(btn => {
      btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
        document.querySelectorAll('.tab-content').forEach(c => c.classList.remove('active'));
        btn.classList.add('active');
        document.getElementById(btn.getAttribute('data-tab')).classList.add('active');
        if (btn.getAttribute('data-tab') === 'tab-logs') refreshLogs();
      });
    });

    async function refreshStatus() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/status');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        document.getElementById('kpi-map').textContent = (d.map || 'PRISONER').toUpperCase();
        document.getElementById('kpi-mode').textContent = `MODO: ${(d.variant || d.gametype || 'SLAYER').toUpperCase()}`;
        document.getElementById('kpi-players').textContent = `${d.players || 0} / ${d.max_players || 128}`;
        document.getElementById('kpi-tick').textContent = `${(d.tickrate || 30.0).toFixed(1)} HZ`;
        document.getElementById('table-count').textContent = `${d.players || 0} PRESENTES`;
        
        // Memoria y Uptime reales
        if (d.rss_kb) {
          const mb = (d.rss_kb / 1024).toFixed(1);
          document.getElementById('kpi-ram').textContent = `${mb} MB`;
        }
        if (d.uptime) {
          const hrs = Math.floor(d.uptime / 3600);
          const mins = Math.floor((d.uptime % 3600) / 60);
          document.getElementById('kpi-uptime').textContent = `UPTIME: ${hrs}h ${mins}m`;
        }
        if (d.node_info) {
          document.getElementById('node-env-tag').textContent = `NODE: ${d.node_info} · NETCODE: V${d.network_version || 39}`;
        }
        if (d.name) {
          document.getElementById('host-badge').textContent = `HOST: ${d.name}`;
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function refreshPlayers() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/players');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        const tbody = document.getElementById('players-body');
        if (!d.players || d.players.length === 0) {
          tbody.innerHTML = '<tr><td colspan="6" style="text-align:center;color:var(--text-muted);padding:24px;">NO HAY JUGADORES HUMANOS CONECTADOS.</td></tr>';
          return;
        }
        tbody.innerHTML = d.players.map(p => `
          <tr>
            <td>[${p.slot}]</td>
            <td><strong>${p.name}</strong></td>
            <td>${p.team === 0 ? 'ROJO' : 'AZUL'}</td>
            <td>${p.score || 0}</td>
            <td>${p.ping || 0} ms</td>
            <td style="text-align:right;">
              <button class="hud-btn" style="padding:2px 8px;font-size:12px;" onclick="execHs('kick ${p.name}')">KICK</button>
              <button class="hud-btn hud-btn-red" style="padding:2px 8px;font-size:12px;" onclick="execHs('ban ${p.name}')">BAN</button>
            </td>
          </tr>
        `).join('');
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function refreshLogs() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/log');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        const out = document.getElementById('logs-output');
        if (d.lines && d.lines.length > 0) {
          out.textContent = d.lines.join('\n');
          out.scrollTop = out.scrollHeight;
        } else {
          out.textContent = 'NO HAY ENTRADAS DE LOG DISPONIBLES EN DEBUG.TXT';
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function loadSettings() {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/settings');
        if (!res.ok) return;
        const d = await res.json();
        if (d.settings) {
          d.settings.forEach(s => {
            if (s.name === 'network.server_name') document.getElementById('cfg-name').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'debug.network_test_countdown') document.getElementById('cfg-countdown').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'debug.network_test_time') document.getElementById('cfg-time').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'server.region') {
              document.getElementById('cfg-region').value = s.value;
              document.getElementById('region-badge').textContent = `ONLINE · ${s.value.toUpperCase()}`;
            }
            if (s.name === 'server.chat_filter') document.getElementById('cfg-filter').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'network.map_rotation') document.getElementById('cfg-rot-mode').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'network.afk_timeout') document.getElementById('cfg-afk').value = s.value;
            if (s.name === 'webhooks.discord') document.getElementById('cfg-discord').value = s.value || '';
            if (s.name === 'webhooks.telegram') document.getElementById('cfg-telegram').value = s.value || '';
          });
        }
      } catch (e) {}
    }

    async function saveSettings() {
      const payload = {
        "network.server_name": document.getElementById('cfg-name').value,
        "debug.network_test_countdown": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-countdown').value) || 1,
        "debug.network_test_time": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-time').value) || 15,
        "server.region": document.getElementById('cfg-region').value,
        "server.chat_filter": document.getElementById('cfg-filter').value,
        "network.map_rotation": document.getElementById('cfg-rot-mode').value,
        "network.afk_timeout": parseInt(document.getElementById('cfg-afk').value) || 180,
        "webhooks.discord": document.getElementById('cfg-discord').value,
        "webhooks.telegram": document.getElementById('cfg-telegram').value
      };
      try {
        await fetch('/api/settings', {
          method: 'PUT',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify(payload)
        });
        showToast('PARAMETROS APLICADOS EN CALIENTE');
        refreshStatus();
      } catch (e) {
        showToast('ERROR AL APLICAR');
      }
    }

    async function execHs(cmd) {
      try {
        await fetch('/api/command', {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ line: cmd })
        });
        showToast('COMANDO EJECUTADO: ' + cmd);
        logCli('> ' + cmd + ' [OK]');
      } catch (e) {
        showToast('ERROR AL EJECUTAR');
      }
    }

    function execPlayer(action) {
      const name = document.getElementById('mod-target').value.trim();
      if (!name) return;
      execHs(action + ' ' + name);
      document.getElementById('mod-target').value = '';
    }

    function sendCli() {
      const inp = document.getElementById('cli-input');
      const val = inp.value.trim();
      if (!val) return;
      execHs(val);
      inp.value = '';
    }

    function logCli(text) {
      const out = document.getElementById('cli-output');
      out.textContent += '\n' + text;
      out.scrollTop = out.scrollHeight;
    }

    function showToast(text) {
      const t = document.getElementById('hud-toast');
      t.textContent = text;
      t.style.display = 'block';
      setTimeout(() => { t.style.display = 'none'; }, 2500);
    }

    document.getElementById('btn-save-ops').addEventListener('click', saveSettings);
    document.getElementById('btn-save-full').addEventListener('click', saveSettings);
    document.getElementById('btn-skip').addEventListener('click', async () => {
      await fetch('/api/rotation/play', { method: 'POST' });
      showToast('SALTANDO A SIGUIENTE PARTIDA...');
      setTimeout(refreshStatus, 1500);
    });
    document.getElementById('btn-shuffle').addEventListener('click', () => execHs('sv_map beavercreek slayer'));
    document.getElementById('btn-stop').addEventListener('click', () => execHs('sv_end_game'));

    setInterval(refreshStatus, 3000);
    setInterval(refreshPlayers, 3000);
    refreshStatus();
    refreshPlayers();
    loadSettings();
  </script>
</body>
</html>

```

`docs/anticheat.md`:

```md
# Anti-Cheat Audit and Host Security Model

This document specifies the security and authority architecture of the OpenCE dedicated server (network version 38). It documents every protection mechanism, whether authority resides on the host or client, the exact implementation locations in source code, verified operational limits, and instructions for server operators.

---

## Executive Summary

Halo CE's distributed network model in OpenCE is hybrid: **server-authoritative simulation with client-side prediction and lag-compensated hit registration**.

1. **Damage Authority**: Damage is dealt exclusively by the host (`network_damage.c:7-8`). Clients report candidate hits (`_distributed_message_hit_reports`). The host strictly audits each report against weapon ownership, firing rate limits, line-of-sight geometry, historical trajectory, bounding spheres, and time bounds (`network_damage.c:2061-2295`). Clients cannot inflict arbitrary damage or fabricate weapon damage types they do not possess.
2. **Weapons and Inventory Authority**: All inventories, carried weapons, total ammunition, and loaded rounds are completely authoritative on the host (`network_objects.c:1602-1634`). The host sends inventory states down to clients (`_distributed_message_inventories`); clients never dictate their ammunition or grenade counts to the host.
3. **Score Authority**: Kills, deaths, team scores, and game objectives are computed solely by the host (`network_distributed.c:29, 4735-4746`).
4. **Movement and Speed Validation**: Client movement is predicted locally, but the host validates unit speed, jump velocities, and flight ceilings each tick (`network_distributed.c:2181-2299, 2429-2524`). Clock manipulation (speed hacking) is monitored over sliding 2-second windows with automatic prediction refusal and stream-verified bans (`network_distributed.c:4357-4456`).

---

## Protection Matrix

| System / Vector | Authority Model | Host Enforcement Evidence | Vulnerability / Spoof Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Damage Execution** | Host Authoritative | `network_damage.c:7-8, 2333-2337` | **Enforced**. Clients cannot apply direct damage; only host calls `object_cause_damage`. |
| **Hit Report Validation** | Host Audited | `network_damage.c:2061-2295` | **Enforced**. Validates weapon held, rate of fire, distance reach, LoS raycast, target history, and time bounds. |
| **Damage Reach & Range** | Host Audited | `network_damage.c:1745-1776, 2154-2160, 2204-2209` | **Enforced**. Projectile flight envelope and bounding radius checked against weapon tag limits. |
| **Line-of-Sight Check** | Host Audited | `network_damage.c:1988-2046, 2233-2248` | **Enforced**. World structure raycast (`collision_test_line`) prevents shooting through solid geometry. |
| **Weapon Firing Rates** | Host Audited | `network_damage.c:110-120, 2173-2175` | **Enforced**. Rate bucket (`HIT_REPORT_BURST_SECONDS`) caps hit frequency to tag trigger rates. |
| **Inventory & Ammo** | Host Authoritative | `network_objects.c:1602-1634, 3008-3058` | **Enforced**. Host simulates magazines and grenades; client takes host inventory. |
| **Scores & Statistics** | Host Authoritative | `network_distributed.c:29, 4735-4746` | **Enforced**. Score delta messages from clients do not exist. |
| **Speed Hack (Clock)** | Host Monitored | `network_distributed.c:4357-4456` | **Enforced**. Refuses predictions at >1.1x speed; bans at 10 s sustained stream-verified skew. |
| **Movement & Flying** | Host Clamped | `network_distributed.c:2181-2299, 2469-2504` | **Enforced**. Client positions clamped to tag biped speed, jump velocity, and fall rates. |
| **Teleportation** | Host Clamped | `network_distributed.c:2469` | **Enforced**. Delta positions > `HOST_ACCEPT_TOLERANCE` (3.0 world units) rejected. |
| **Bans & Identity** | Host Enforced | `network_distributed.c:4247-4290` | **Enforced**. IP and hardware ID checked against `bans.txt` on connection. |
| **Vote-Kick Integrity** | Host Stream-Gated | `network_distributed.c:4619-4629`, `network_votekick.c` | **Enforced**. Only accepted from reliable stream; counted by unique IP and HWID. |
| **Aimbot / Memory Injection** | Client Memory | N/A (Client Execution) | **Not Protected by Host**. Host cannot detect external memory manipulation or aim snapping. |

---

## Detailed Audit Findings

### 1. Damage Reach and Hit Report Validation

#### Test Harness vs Production Path
The distance checks in `port/linux/game/network_test.c:568-580` (`network_test_shoot`) are exclusive to the debug harness (`debug.network_test_shoot` / `HALO_NETWORK_TEST_SHOOT`) used by `tools/net_compare.py`. They never execute during normal server hosting.

However, the production damage pipeline in `port/linux/game/network_damage.c` implements comprehensive, server-side validation:
1. **Report Origin and Ownership** (`network_damage.c:2085-2090`): Host verifies that the reporting machine owns the player claimed as the damage dealer.
2. **Weapon Ownership Verification** (`network_damage.c:2118-2121`, `1262-1329`): Host inspects the player's recent weapon history (`damage_players[player].definition_indices`) within `RECENT_WEAPON_TICKS` (10 seconds / 300 ticks). If the damage effect tag does not match a weapon or projectile currently or recently held by the player, the report is rejected (`rate <= 0.0f`).
3. **Grenade Consumption** (`network_damage.c:2161-2171`, `2179-2180`): Grenade damage is accepted only if the host witnessed the player throw a grenade (`distributed_grenade_throw`) of that type within the valid time window. Once detonated, the recorded throw is consumed (`damage_players[player].throw_times[throw_index] = NONE`).
4. **Burst Rate Limiting** (`network_damage.c:2173-2175`): Weapon hit reports are metered by `distributed_report_paid` against the weapon trigger's rate of fire with a 3-second burst tolerance (`HIT_REPORT_BURST_SECONDS = 3`, `HIT_REPORT_RATE_MARGIN = 2`). Flooding hit reports beyond tag firing parameters fails validation.
5. **Melee Distance and Origin** (`network_damage.c:2184-2188`, `1675-1697`): Melee damage requires the host's historical trail of the player's unit position (`distributed_player_was_near`) within the target history buffer to be in proximity to both the impact origin and the epicenter.
6. **Vehicle Collision Verification** (`network_damage.c:2197-2201`, `1704-1737`): Damage from vehicle impact requires the host to confirm that the reporting player was driving the vehicle and that the vehicle trajectory intercepted the target within bounding sphere radii.
7. **Projectile Flight Reach** (`network_damage.c:2204-2209`, `1745-1776`): Point damage (bullets, projectiles) must lie within the reach distance (`damage_reach.distance`) calculated from tag velocity and maximum lifetime (`distributed_projectile_flight`), measured from anywhere the player has been along the historical movement trail (`damage_trails`).
8. **Target Historical Window (Lag Compensation)** (`network_damage.c:2213-2230`): Target position reported by the client is verified against the host's object history buffer (`damage_history`, 64 ticks / ~2.13 s). If the target was not near that position within `REPORT_MAXIMUM_AGE_TICKS` (30 ticks / 1.0 s), the report is rejected.
9. **Line-of-Sight Raycasting** (`network_damage.c:2233-2248`, `1988-2046`): Before applying point damage, the host traces collision rays (`collision_test_line` with `_collision_test_structure_bit`) between the shooter's historical eye positions and the target bounding sphere. If solid world geometry occludes all line-of-sight paths, the damage is discarded.

### 2. Ammunition and Grenade Authority

- **Inventory Transmission**: The host packages unit inventory state in `distributed_inventory_from_unit` (`network_objects.c:1602-1634`) and transmits it via `_distributed_message_inventories` (`network_objects.c:1783-1790`).
- **Client Handling**: Clients receive inventory packets in `network_objects_handle_inventories` (`network_objects.c:3166-3175`) and overwrite local magazine and grenade state via `distributed_client_apply_inventory` (`network_objects.c:3008-3058`).
- **No Client-to-Host Inventory Packet**: In `network_distributed.c:4617-4638`, `_distributed_message_inventories` is processed exclusively by clients (`game_connection() == _game_connection_network_client`). If a rogue client sends an inventory message to the host, it is ignored and dropped.
- **Weapon Firing**: Weapon firing is simulated on the host by feeding player input actions (`update_server_handle_distributed_input`, `network_distributed.c:2850`). Ammo is deducted server-side by weapon simulation routines.

### 3. Score and Objective Authority

- **Host Simulation**: Kill attribution and deaths are registered by the host in `network_damage.c` and recorded in `distributed_deaths` (`network_distributed.c:3340-3423`).
- **Statistics Broadcast**: Every tick or whenever statistics change, the host broadcasts `_distributed_message_player_statistics` (`network_distributed.c:3596-3671`).
- **Client Reception**: Clients update scoreboard numbers in `network_distributed.c:4735-4746`. Clients have no message type to report scores, kills, or objective captures to the host.

### 4. Movement and Speed Hack Detection

#### Speed Hack Detection Engine
Implemented in `network_distributed.c:4357-4456` (`distributed_note_client_clock`):
- **Measurement Window**: Measured over 2000 ms sliding windows (`CLIENT_CLOCK_WINDOW_MILLISECONDS = 2000`).
- **Rate Threshold**: Clock rate exceeding 1.10x real time (`CLIENT_CLOCK_FAST_RATE = 1.1f`).
- **Ahead Threshold**: Client clock more than 15 ticks (0.50 s) ahead of host time (`CLIENT_CLOCK_AHEAD_TICKS = 15`).
- **Immediate Penalty**: When both conditions are met, the machine is flagged `clock->fast = TRUE`. During this time, `distributed_machine_clock_fast(machine_index)` causes `network_distributed.c:4664` to immediately drop all incoming `_distributed_message_player_prediction` and `_distributed_message_vehicle_prediction` packets. The host simulates the player using server-side ticks only.
- **Auto-Kick / Ban Duration**: 5 consecutive fast windows (`CLIENT_CLOCK_FAST_WINDOWS = 5`, 10 seconds total).
- **Stream Confirmation**: To prevent UDP source IP spoofing from maliciously disconnecting other players, the host requires confirmation on the reliable TCP/TLS stream (`clock->ahead_on_stream = TRUE`, `network_distributed.c:4368-4369, 4399`). If fast clock ticks are observed only in UDP datagrams, the player is not dropped; an unverified warning is logged to `cheaters.txt` (`network_distributed.c:4434-4450`).

#### Movement Validation Bounds
Implemented in `network_distributed.c:2181-2299` (`distributed_on_foot_bound`) and `2429-2524` (`distributed_take_prediction`):
- **Maximum Step Distance**: Target position delta between ticks must not exceed `HOST_ACCEPT_TOLERANCE` (3.0 world units, `network_distributed.c:2469`).
- **Horizontal & Vertical Velocity**: Velocity is bounded by `run_speed`, `jump_speed`, and double-speed traits (`network_distributed.c:2251-2272`).
- **Ceiling Clamping**: Z-height is restricted by `distributed_on_foot_ceiling` (`network_distributed.c:2496-2500`). Floating or flying above legitimate jump and explosive knockback arcs is rejected.

---

## Operator Guide: Bans, Cheater Logs, and Recovery

### File Locations on Linux

The server engine references files using Xbox drive paths:
- `d:\bans.txt`
- `d:\cheaters.txt`

Under the Linux platform abstraction layer (`port/linux/src/xbox_files.c:6-17` and `port/linux/src/msvc_crt.c:578-583`), `d:\` translates to the **data root**:
1. Directory path configured by `paths.data` in `config.toml`.
2. Or current working directory if it contains a `maps/` folder.
3. In the official Docker container and server deployment layout, these files are written to the server runtime directory:
   - `/root/halo-server-pkg/server/bans.txt` (or `/app/server/bans.txt` in container volume).
   - `/root/halo-server-pkg/server/cheaters.txt`.

### File Format

Entries are written as single-line ASCII records (`network_distributed.c:4184-4228`):
```text
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS ip=<ip_address> hwid=<32_hex_chars> discord="<username>" (<discord_id>) name="<player_name>" reason="<reason>"
```

Example:
```text
2026-10-24 21:05:12 ip=198.51.100.42 hwid=a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90 discord="spartan" (123456789012345678) name="MasterChief" reason="speed hack (game ran 1.45 times as fast)"
```

### Unbanning a Player

The ban list is checked upon connection in `network_distributed_banned` (`network_distributed.c:4249-4290`):
1. Open `bans.txt` in any text editor.
2. Locate the line containing the target IP or HWID.
3. Delete the line and save the file.
4. Changes take effect on subsequent connection attempts (the file is re-read on every incoming connection handshake).

### Diagnosing Network Lag and Clock False Positives

Players on unstable links, cellular connections, or behind Carrier-Grade NAT (CGNAT) may experience sudden burst packet delivery.
- **Why False Positives are Rare**: A delayed burst may cause ticks to arrive quickly, but `clock->latest_tick - game_time_get()` will not remain sustained ahead of the host clock for 10 continuous seconds. Furthermore, unverified UDP packet bursts alone never trigger an auto-kick (`network_distributed.c:4429-4435`).
- **Symptom of Real Speed Hack**: Consistent logging in `debug.txt` showing `machine #N's game runs X.XX times as fast as this host's` across 5 consecutive windows (10 s), accompanied by stream verification.
- **Symptom of Network Jitter / Packet Delivery Burst**: An isolated log entry `datagrams said its game ran X times as fast... its stream not: not dropped (unverified)`. If an operator sees unverified warnings without actual speed hack kicks, the player is experiencing bufferbloat or connection reordering, not running a cheat.

---

## Known Gaps and Unprotected Vectors

The following vectors are not protected by the dedicated server engine:

| Vector | Severity | Explanation | Mitigation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Client-Side Aimbot / Auto-Aim** | **High** | Clients compute their own input pitch and yaw angles locally. Memory injection or aim assistance tools that lock onto player bounding boxes cannot be detected server-side. | Operator observation, player vote-kick (`votekick <player>`), and community reports. |
| **Wallhack / ESP (Entity Display)** | **High** | OpenCE sends player positions within network visibility zones to all clients for smooth local interpolation. Client memory scanners can read unit coordinates and render ESP overlays. | Fast kick/ban via operator console; player vote-kicking. |
| **HWID Spoofing** | **Medium** | The client generates its hardware ID locally (`p2p_hardware_id`). A malicious actor running with administrative privileges can modify `/etc/machine-id` or spoof SMBIOS data to generate a new HWID. | Combined IP banning + server password gating (`network.server_password`). |
| **Public Chat Forced Off Bug** | **Low** | In public listed games, text chat was historically forced off in `chat_host_config_flags`. | Resolved in Milestone 2 (`network.public_chat = true`). |

---

## Conclusion

The OpenCE dedicated server engine exhibits rigorous server authority across all gameplay-critical states: hits are raycast-verified and history-bounded, inventories and ammunition are completely host-simulated, scores cannot be modified by clients, and clock manipulations trigger automated prediction revocation and kicking.

No engine code changes are required for anti-cheat verification in Milestone 4.

```

`docs/dedicated_server.md`:

```md
# A dedicated server

A copy of the game can be left running as a host: it hosts a list of maps on its own,
starts its games, returns to its lobby after each one, and the machines that join are told
what the game has left. Players get in with an invite link or find it in the server
browser.

There is no central server. This is one copy of the game holding a game open for others,
which is the automated system link host the port already has (`debug.network_test`,
`port/linux/NETCODE.md`), given a map list.

## Platforms

The same host, the same `config.toml` and the same netcode, on both platforms the game
builds for as a desktop executable:

| Platform | Build it | Run it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux, x86 32-bit | `python configure.py` then `ninja linux`, or the CI's `dist/halo-linux-release/` | `./halo` |
| Windows, x86 32-bit | `ninja windows` (native, or `--windows-cross` from Linux), or the CI's `dist/halo-windows-release/` | `halo.exe` |

Both are the same game: a server started on Windows and one started on Linux hold the
same games, take the same clients and read the same settings, and a client of one platform
joins a server of the other. The settings' names, the map list's syntax, the log and the
invite link are identical; only the way each system keeps the process running differs
(below, "Keep it running").

It needs no screen, no GPU and no audio device: the renderer is null and the audio is
off, so a machine with neither a display nor a sound card runs it as it is. The Android
app and the web build are clients: the app can host a game while it runs, but it has no
headless mode, and a browser tab is closed with the page.

## What it needs

- A build of the game, of the platform the machine runs (above).
- The game data: a folder that contains `maps/`, as when playing.
- A `config.toml` beside the executable with the settings below. The game writes the file
  with its defaults at the first start, and a key that is wrong is written to the log and
  left at its default.
- A machine that stays on, and one UDP port for Internet play: set `network.tunnel_port`
  to a fixed one (2302 below), so that the firewall's rule and the router's forward name
  it; 0 (the default) lets the game pick a different port at each start. The game asks the
  router to forward it by itself (UPnP), so an ordinary connection works; **it is one port
  per machine**, so two copies of the game cannot both host Internet play on one
  machine.

## The settings

The same file on both platforms, in the sections the settings belong to:

```toml
[debug]
# a server has no screen: nothing is drawn, no window is made
null_renderer = true

# the map list it hosts, in the order to play it: entries of "map" or
# "map:variant,variant,...", ";" between them, and back to the first past the
# last. Map names are the ones the game's map lists show ("levels\test\wizard",
# and a Custom Edition map as "custom_maps\<name>", refer to
# docs/custom_edition_caches.md)
network_test = "host:wizard:slayer,ctf;chillout:slayer,ctf,oddball;sidewinder:ctf,slayer"

# the minutes every game of the list lasts, so a game nobody wins still ends
# and the list moves on
network_test_time = 15

# the seconds its lobby counts down to the start of a game. 0: the game's own,
# 31 seconds
network_test_countdown = 15

# how long the host waits for a countdown before starting a game by force, when
# nothing else starts it
network_test_start = 1.0

# false: the host takes no player of its own. Its games are the players' alone
# and it waits in its lobby for the first one. true (the default) is the
# automated test's host, which plays as a player of its own: every machine
# shows that player, and the games count it
network_test_player = false

[audio]
# no audio device is opened
enabled = false

[paths]
# the data root, when the maps are not beside the executable
# data = "/srv/halo"

[network]
# the name its listing shows in everyone's server browser (32 bytes at most in
# the browser; the in-game lobby shows 15 characters)
server_name = "Joces ESMX 24/7"

# the UDP port internet play uses: a fixed one, so the firewall rule and the
# router's forward name it (0 lets the game pick one at each start)
tunnel_port = 2302

[display]
# tell the players, in the chat area, how much of the game is left and the
# lobby count down. Each machine works it out from the game's options and its
# clock, so nothing new goes between them
time_notices = true
```

Each setting has an environment variable that overrides the file for one start; they are
in the settings table of `port/linux/README.md` (the same names on Windows) and explained
in `port/linux/NETCODE.md`. On Windows, set them in the shell that starts the server, or
in a `.cmd` wrapper:

```bat
set HALO_DATA_ROOT=C:\halo
set HALO_NULL_RENDERER=1
set HALO_NO_AUDIO=1
halo.exe
```

## Run it

Enter the executable, from the folder of the data:

```
cd /srv/halo
./halo
```

```
cd C:\halo
halo.exe
```

The game writes its invite link (a `halo://join/<64 hexadecimal digits>` line) to the
standard error at the start of every hosting, and logs the rest to the standard output and
to its own log.

## Keep it running

**Linux**, a unit that keeps it running and restarts it:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Halo: Combat Evolved dedicated server
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=halo
WorkingDirectory=/srv/halo
Environment=HALO_DATA_ROOT=/srv/halo
ExecStart=/srv/halo/halo
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

**Windows**, either in a console window that stays open (minimized is enough), or as a
service with a wrapper such as NSSM, or a task of Task Scheduler started at logon with
"Do not stop the task if it runs longer than" unchecked. The executable has the same
settings and the same null renderer, so nothing of it shows.

On both, keep the machine from sleeping (Linux: `systemd-inhibit` or mask
`sleep.target`; Windows: the power plan's sleep set to never, only for the server's
account).

## Open the port

```
# Linux (ufw)
ufw allow 2302/udp

# Windows (an elevated prompt)
netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Halo CE server" dir=in action=allow protocol=UDP localport=2302
```

## What it does, and what to expect

- **It lists itself** in everyone's server browser under `network.server_name`, and prints
  its invite link, which changes on every start.
- **It waits in its lobby** for the first player, with the next entry of its list set and
  pre-cached. The countdown starts when a player is in (one player with nobody else is
  enough), and the game begins exactly as the countdown reaches zero.
- **Every game it plays ends and the list moves on**, whether the score, the time limit or
  the last player leaving ends it. A game whose players have all left is closed fifteen
  seconds after the last one (a grace: a connection that comes back inside them keeps the
  game it was in), and a variant of the list that asks for teams, with fewer than two
  players in the game, plays as that map's first variant that does not.
- **It keeps its listing** while it operates, and comes back to its lobby after every game
  instead of dropping the game it holds.
- **An operator can watch it** without a screen: its state, and how much of the game it is
  running is left, go to the log every five seconds, together with the reasons a countdown
  is not running, the machines joining and leaving, and the messages between them
  (`debug.txt`, the engine's own log, and the standard output).

```
server: state 1 (pregame 0, ingame 1, postgame 2), map levels\test\wizard\wizard,
14 of 15 minutes left after 61 s, countdown active, 0 ms left;
machines 1, a player on each 1, teams 1, players 2 of 1, all pre-cached 1
```

## Who can join

A client joins a host whose network version is in its range
(`HALO_PORT_NETWORK_VERSION_MINIMUM` to `HALO_PORT_NETWORK_VERSION_MAXIMUM`): its own,
and those that differ from it only in what the other machine drops. In this build the
range is 38 alone, so a client of 38 joins it and one of another version does not
(`port/linux/NETCODE.md`, "Versions"). The range is the client's: a host never checks a
client's version, and an
old client that only knows its own version refuses a newer host until it is updated. A
machine that joins in the middle of a game plays it from where it is, and a machine that
joins the lobby is counted for the next one.

## Notes

- The settings above belong to the automated system link host. With their defaults (no map
  list, no notices, the test's own player) nothing of this operates and a host the menus
  make is the one the game always had.
- One host per machine: the Internet play port is one, and so is the copy of the game the
  links of `halo://` open.
- The games are the game's own: a dedicated host does not change what a map or a gametype
  does, only which one comes next.

```

```md
# Guía de Registro en el Master Server

Esta guía detalla el procedimiento para registrar un servidor dedicado ante el Master Server oficial de OpenCE (`master.opencommunityedition.com`).

A partir de OpenCE Build 289, los servidores dedicados que se muestran en la pestaña oficial **DEDICATED** del explorador del juego requieren autenticación criptográfica mediante un par de claves Ed25519 registradas ante el bot oficial de verificación. Los servidores no autenticados permanecen descubribles mediante brokers de señalización P2P en el explorador general, pero no aparecerán en la categoría verificada DEDICATED sin completar este flujo de validación.

---

## 1. Generación de Claves Criptográficas (`--keygen`)

El motor OpenCE utiliza firmas asimétricas Ed25519 para verificar la identidad del servidor. Antes de solicitar el registro, genere un par de claves de publisher en la máquina anfitriona.

### Ejecución

Ejecute el binario `halo` desde el directorio de instalación del servidor utilizando el argumento `--keygen`:

```bash
./halo --keygen
```

### Gestión de Claves y Políticas de Seguridad

1. **Generación de Archivos**: El motor genera un archivo de clave de 64 bytes denominado `publisher.key` en el directorio de trabajo actual, junto con la correspondiente clave pública en formato hexadecimal.
2. **Permisos**: Configure permisos estrictos en el sistema de archivos inmediatamente para prevenir compromisos de la clave privada:
   ```bash
   chmod 600 publisher.key
   ```
3. **Directivas de OPSEC**:
   - Nunca envíe `publisher.key` a repositorios de control de versiones.
   - Nunca exponga `publisher.key` a través de directorios públicos, dashboards web o registros de contenedores.
   - Restrinja el acceso de lectura estrictamente al usuario del sistema que ejecuta el proceso del servidor.

---

## 2. Solicitud de Registro en Discord (`/apply`)

El registro del servidor se coordina a través del bot de operaciones del Master Server de OpenCE alojado en el servidor oficial de Discord.

### Procedimiento Paso a Paso

1. Únase al servidor oficial de Discord de la comunidad OpenCE.
2. Diríjase al canal `#master-server-registration` o al canal designado para interacciones con el bot.
3. Ejecute el comando de barra diagonal `/apply`:
   ```text
   /apply public_key:<CLAVE_PUBLICA_HEX> server_name:<NOMBRE_DEL_SERVIDOR>
   ```
4. El bot del Master Server valida el formato de la clave pública y emite una cadena de desafío criptográfico denominada **nonce** (una cadena hexadecimal aleatoria de alta entropía y de un solo uso).
5. Copie la cadena exacta del nonce proporcionada en la respuesta del bot. El desafío expira tras una ventana de tiempo fija (habitualmente 15 minutos).

---

## 3. Prueba Criptográfica de Posesión (`--sign`)

Para demostrar la posesión de la clave privada correspondiente a la clave pública enviada, firme el nonce de desafío mediante la CLI del motor `halo`.

### Firma del Desafío

Ejecute el binario `halo` utilizando el parámetro `--sign` seguido del nonce exacto recibido del bot:

```bash
./halo --sign "<nonce>"
```

### Salida del Comando

El binario lee `publisher.key` del directorio de trabajo, calcula la firma Ed25519 sobre el desafío y muestra la firma resultante en la salida estándar:

```text
nonce:     a8f9c1d2e3b4...
signature: 5f8a9b2c...3d1e
```

### Conclusión del Protocolo de Verificación

1. Regrese al canal de registro en Discord.
2. Envíe la prueba de firma mediante el comando de verificación indicado por el bot:
   ```text
   /verify nonce:<nonce> signature:<FIRMA_HEX>
   ```
3. Una vez validada la firma contra la clave pública registrada, el bot confirma la autorización:
   ```text
   Server identity verified. Publisher authorized for official DEDICATED listings.
   ```

---

## 4. Configuración del Servidor y Verificación en la Lista Master

Tras obtener la aprobación del registro, configure el archivo del servidor dedicado para declarar la ubicación geográfica y establecer la comunicación con el master server.

### Configuración (`server/config.toml`)

Abra `server/config.toml` (o suministre las variables de entorno equivalentes) y configure los parámetros de identidad:

```toml
[network]
online = true
host_public = true
tunnel_port = 2302

# Identificador de Región del Servidor
# Se muestra en la columna de ping/región del Server Browser.
# Opciones válidas: "eu", "na-e", "na-w", "sa", "ap-e", "ap-s", "af"
region = "eu"
```

Alternativa con variables de entorno:
```bash
export HALO_SERVER_REGION="eu"
export HALO_NET_ONLINE="true"
export HALO_NET_HOST_PUBLIC="true"
```

### Requisitos de Red

El Master Server ejecuta una prueba de conectividad activa contra el anfitrión para verificar la accesibilidad de los clientes antes de incorporar el nodo al directorio público:

- Verifique que el puerto UDP `2302` (o el configurado en `network.tunnel_port`) se encuentre abierto y redireccionado en su cortafuegos/enrutador.
- Confirme conectividad de salida hacia el puerto HTTPS `443` de `master.opencommunityedition.com`.

### Verificación de la Publicación

1. Inicie el servicio del servidor dedicado:
   ```bash
   ./halo
   ```
2. Inspeccione la salida de registro de inicio para comprobar el enlace con el master server:
   ```text
   server_master: publishing identity to master.opencommunityedition.com...
   server_master: published to master.opencommunityedition.com (200 OK)
   ```
3. Inicie el cliente de juego OpenCE (Build 289 o superior).
4. Diríjase a **Multiplayer** > **Internet**.
5. Cambie a la pestaña **DEDICATED**.
6. Confirme que su servidor aparece en el listado con el nombre configurado, capacidad de jugadores, indicadores de latencia y la etiqueta de región asignada (por ejemplo, `EU`).

```md
# Master Server Registration Guide

This guide details the procedure for registering a dedicated server with the official OpenCE Master Server (`master.opencommunityedition.com`).

Starting with OpenCE Build 289, dedicated servers displayed under the in-game **DEDICATED** browser tab require cryptographic authentication using an Ed25519 keypair registered with the official registry bot. Unauthenticated servers remain discoverable via public P2P signaling brokers under the general browser, but will not appear in the verified DEDICATED category without completing this verification workflow.

---

## 1. Cryptographic Key Generation (`--keygen`)

The OpenCE engine utilizes asymmetric Ed25519 signatures for server identity verification. Before applying for registration, generate a unique publisher keypair on your host machine.

### Execution

Run the `halo` binary from your server installation directory using the `--keygen` argument:

```bash
./halo --keygen
```

### Key Management and Security Policies

1. **File Generation**: The engine generates a 64-byte key file named `publisher.key` in the current working directory, alongside the corresponding public key in hexadecimal format.
2. **Permissions**: Set strict filesystem permissions immediately to avoid private key compromise:
   ```bash
   chmod 600 publisher.key
   ```
3. **OPSEC Directives**:
   - Never commit `publisher.key` to version control repositories.
   - Never expose `publisher.key` through public directories, web dashboards, or container logs.
   - Restrict read access strictly to the system user executing the server process.

---

## 2. Discord Master Server Application (`/apply`)

Server registration is coordinated through the OpenCE Master Server operations bot hosted in the official Discord guild.

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. Join the official OpenCE Community Discord server.
2. Navigate to the `#master-server-registration` or dedicated bot interaction channel.
3. Execute the `/apply` slash command:
   ```text
   /apply public_key:<YOUR_HEX_PUBLIC_KEY> server_name:<YOUR_SERVER_NAME>
   ```
4. The Master Server bot validates the public key format and issues a cryptographic challenge string called a **nonce** (a high-entropy, single-use random hexadecimal string).
5. Copy the exact nonce string provided in the bot's response. The challenge expires after a fixed time window (typically 15 minutes).

---

## 3. Cryptographic Proof of Possession (`--sign`)

To prove ownership of the private key matching the submitted public key, sign the challenge nonce with the `halo` engine CLI.

### Signing the Challenge

Execute the `halo` binary using the `--sign` flag followed by the exact nonce string received from the bot:

```bash
./halo --sign "<nonce>"
```

### Response Output

The binary reads `publisher.key` from the working directory, computes the Ed25519 signature over the challenge payload, and prints the resulting signature to standard output:

```text
nonce:     a8f9c1d2e3b4...
signature: 5f8a9b2c...3d1e
```

### Completing the Handshake

1. Return to the registration channel on Discord.
2. Submit the signature proof using the verification command prompted by the bot:
   ```text
   /verify nonce:<nonce> signature:<SIGNATURE_HEX>
   ```
3. Once the signature is validated against the registered public key, the bot issues confirmation:
   ```text
   Server identity verified. Publisher authorized for official DEDICATED listings.
   ```

---

## 4. Server Configuration and Master Listing Verification

After registration approval, configure your dedicated server configuration file to declare geographic location and establish communications with the master server.

### Configuration (`server/config.toml`)

Open `server/config.toml` (or pass the equivalent environment variables) and set the identity parameters:

```toml
[network]
online = true
host_public = true
tunnel_port = 2302

# Server Region Identifier
# Displayed in the Server Browser ping/region column.
# Valid options: "eu", "na-e", "na-w", "sa", "ap-e", "ap-s", "af"
region = "eu"
```

Environment variable alternative:
```bash
export HALO_SERVER_REGION="eu"
export HALO_NET_ONLINE="true"
export HALO_NET_HOST_PUBLIC="true"
```

### Network Requirements

The Master Server performs an active health probe against your host to verify client reachability before adding the node to the public directory:

- Ensure UDP port `2302` (or the configured `network.tunnel_port`) is open and forwarded through your gateway/firewall.
- Confirm stateful egress connectivity to HTTPS port `443` on `master.opencommunityedition.com`.

### Verifying the Listing

1. Start your dedicated server daemon:
   ```bash
   ./halo
   ```
2. Inspect the startup log output for the master publication handshake:
   ```text
   server_master: publishing identity to master.opencommunityedition.com...
   server_master: published to master.opencommunityedition.com (200 OK)
   ```
3. Launch the OpenCE game client (Build 289 or newer).
4. Navigate to **Multiplayer** > **Internet**.
5. Switch to the **DEDICATED** tab.
6. Confirm your server appears in the list with the configured name, player slots, low latency indicators, and the assigned region label (e.g., `EU`).

```

```md
# Operator Console Guide

The dedicated server includes a local telnet administration console and the `scripts/operator.sh` management CLI for operator administration without requiring an in-game client or display.

---

## 1. Enabling the Telnet Console

The console listens on `127.0.0.1:2323` by default (local loopback only, unauthenticated).

### Configuration (`config.toml`)
In `config.toml` under `[debug]`:
```toml
[debug]
telnet_console = true
telnet_console_port = 2323
```

### Environment Variable
Alternatively, pass `HALO_TELNET_CONSOLE=1` (or `true`) at startup:
```bash
HALO_TELNET_CONSOLE=1 ./halo
```

---

## 2. Operator CLI (`scripts/operator.sh`)

`scripts/operator.sh` provides a unified CLI for controlling the dedicated server.

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `operator.sh kick <name>` | Immediately disconnects a player. The player can rejoin. |
| `operator.sh ban <name>` | Drops the player, writes their IP and HWID to `bans.txt` and `cheaters.txt`, and blocks reconnection. |
| `operator.sh votekick <name>` | Triggers a host vote-kick against a player. |
| `operator.sh say <text>` | Broadcast message notice (logs warning: pending native engine chat injection hook). |
| `operator.sh status` | Reads the latest 5-second server state line from `debug.txt` and formats game status. |
| `operator.sh raw <command>` | Sends an arbitrary command or Halo Script expression directly to the console. |

## Text Chat in Public Servers

By default, text chat is disabled in games listed in the public server browser.
A dedicated server with operator moderation can enable it:

In `config.toml`:
```toml
[network]
text_chat = "on"      # on | links | off
public_chat = true    # lift the public-listing restriction
```

With `/mute <name>` (operator chat command) and `operator.sh ban <name>`,
the operator can manage disruptive players. Links are blocked unless
`text_chat = "links"`.

## Server Password (Join Gating)

The dedicated server supports password protection while remaining listed in the public server browser:

In `config.toml`:
```toml
[network]
server_password = "your_secret_password"
```

Or via environment variable:
```bash
export HALO_NET_SERVER_PASSWORD="your_secret_password"
```

### Behavior & Details
- **Empty string (`""`)**: Default. The server is public and open to anyone joining from the browser.
- **Non-empty string**: The server listing is marked as locked (`_listing_password` flag). Its lobby token is sealed with the password key using Argon2id salted with the host signing key (`p2p_seal_token`).
- **Joining**: Clients selecting the locked server in the server browser are prompted for the password (`p2p_listing_unlock`). Only clients entering the correct password can derive the key, unlock the token, and join. Direct invite links continue to work if shared.

## Map Rotation (`map_rotation`)

The dedicated server supports both sequential and pseudo-random rotation across the playlist specified in `debug.network_test`:

In `config.toml`:
```toml
[network]
map_rotation = "sequence"  # "sequence" (default) or "shuffle"
```

Or via environment variable:
```bash
export HALO_NET_MAP_ROTATION="shuffle"
```

### Rotation Modes
- **`sequence`** (default): Rotates through the configured playlist entries and gametype variants sequentially, returning to the first map after reaching the end.
- **`shuffle`**: Randomly selects a map and gametype variant from the entire configured playlist after each game concludes, avoiding picking the exact same entry twice consecutively whenever the playlist contains more than one combination.

### Environment Overrides

- `HALO_CONSOLE_HOST`: Console IP (default: `127.0.0.1`)
- `HALO_CONSOLE_PORT`: Console port (default: `2323`)
- `HALO_LOG_FILE`: Engine log file path for `status` (default: `/root/.local/share/halo-linux/debug.txt`)

### Usage Examples

```bash
# Kick a player
scripts/operator.sh kick "RedSpartan"

# Ban a player
scripts/operator.sh ban "Griefer99"

# Trigger a vote kick
scripts/operator.sh votekick "AfkPlayer"

# Check server state
scripts/operator.sh status
# Output: map: bloodgulch | variant: slayer | players: 4 | state: in_game

# Send raw Halo Script or debug commands
scripts/operator.sh raw "help kick"
```

---

## 3. Docker Usage

When running with Docker or Docker Compose, execute commands inside the container via `docker exec`:

### Enable in `docker-compose.yml`
```yaml
services:
  halo-server:
    image: ghcr.io/joshrob297/halo-ce-server:latest
    environment:
      - HALO_TELNET_CONSOLE=true
```

### Running Commands
```bash
# Check current game status
docker exec halo-server /halo/scripts/operator.sh status

# Kick a player
docker exec halo-server /halo/scripts/operator.sh kick "PlayerName"

# Ban a player
docker exec halo-server /halo/scripts/operator.sh ban "Cheater"

# Send a raw console command
docker exec halo-server /halo/scripts/operator.sh raw "game_won"
```

---

## 4. Bare-Metal Usage

When running bare-metal via systemd or background process:

```bash
# Local execution
/path/to/halo-server-pkg/scripts/operator.sh status

# Remote execution via SSH
ssh user@server '/path/to/halo-server-pkg/scripts/operator.sh kick "PlayerName"'
```

You can also connect directly using `nc` or `socat`:
```bash
printf "kick PlayerName\n" | socat -t 2 - TCP:127.0.0.1:2323
```

---

## 5. Bans and Cheaters Files

Both files are maintained alongside `debug.txt` (typically `/root/.local/share/halo-linux/` or the server execution directory).

### `bans.txt` Format
Each line records a banned entity in tab-delimited format:
```tsv
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS	ip=192.168.1.50	hwid=a1b2c3d4e5f60718	discord_username=none	discord_id=none	players=BadActor	reason=banned by the host
```

- `ip=`: Remote IPv4 address.
- `hwid=`: Sanitized 16-byte hex HMAC-SHA-256 hardware identifier (from Linux machine-id, Windows GUID, or Android ID).
- `discord_username=` / `discord_id=`: Discord identity if self-reported by client.
- `players=`: Player name reported at the time of the ban.
- `reason=`: Reason for the ban (e.g. `banned by the host` or cheater detection details).

### How to Unban
The host checks `bans.txt` on new client connections. To unban a player:
1. Open `bans.txt` in a text editor or remove the corresponding line:
   ```bash
   sed -i '/ip=192.168.1.50/d' /path/to/bans.txt
   ```
2. The change takes effect immediately for subsequent connection attempts.

### `cheaters.txt` Format and Triggers
`cheaters.txt` logs automated anti-cheat detections:
```tsv
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS	ip=192.168.1.75	hwid=f0e1d2c3b4a59687	discord_username=none	discord_id=none	players=SpeedRunner	reason=speed hack detected
```

#### What Triggers an Entry:
1. **Speed Hacks:** The server compares client tick timing against its host clock every 2 seconds. If a client runs >10% faster and >0.5 seconds ahead continuously for 10 seconds, the host automatically drops the connection, bans the IP/HWID in `bans.txt`, and logs the infraction to `cheaters.txt`.
2. **Unverified Timing Discrepancies:** If incoming datagrams are ahead of real time but cannot be confirmed via the client's TCP stream, an `unverified` entry is written to `cheaters.txt` without issuing an immediate ban to protect against packet spoofing.
3. **Manual Host Bans:** When `ban <name>` is executed by the operator, an entry is written to both `bans.txt` and `cheaters.txt`.

---

## 6. Web Dashboard & Health Endpoint

The server includes a zero-dependency, fully embedded HTTP Web Dashboard and REST API on a dedicated TCP port (`network.health_port` in `config.toml` or `HALO_NET_HEALTH_PORT` environment variable, default `:8080`).

Accessing `http://<server-ip>:8080/` in any desktop or mobile browser opens the interactive administration dashboard:
- **Status:** Live match telemetry, game time, live scores, next map, active player count, and 10-minute player history sparkline.
- **Players:** Real-time player listing with ping, team affiliation, IP/HWID, and quick moderation actions (Kick, Ban, Mute).
- **Rotation:** Interactive playlist manager (Up, Down, Remove, Play Now, Add Map).
- **Console (RCON):** Interactive web terminal executing operator commands directly in browser.
- **REST & Health:** Probes requesting `/health` receive instant JSON status responses for uptime monitoring.

The dashboard is built for Linux and Windows only. The Android and web builds
compile it out (their environments have no sockets and threads to spare), so
`network.health_port` is ignored there.

### Configuration

In `config.toml`:
```toml
[network]
health_port = 8080   # Port for the web dashboard and health probe
```

Or via environment variable:
```bash
export HALO_NET_HEALTH_PORT=8080
```

When using Docker Compose, publish the TCP port in `docker-compose.yml`:
```yaml
services:
  halo-server:
    ports:
      - "2302:2302/udp"
      - "8080:8080/tcp"
    environment:
      - HALO_NET_HEALTH_PORT=8080
```

### Endpoints

- `GET /health`: Returns HTTP 200 with JSON status payload:
  ```json
  {"status":"ok","state":"in_game","map":"bloodgulch","variant":"slayer","players":3,"max_players":16,"minutes_left":8,"listed":true,"uptime_seconds":1234}
  ```
State values: `pregame`, `in_game`, `postgame`, `no_server`.

- `HEAD /health`: the same headers with no body, for monitors that probe
  with HEAD.

- Any other path or method: HTTP 404 with `{"error":"not found"}`.

### Example Usage

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
```

The endpoint binds `0.0.0.0` (so a container can publish it), serves no
path but `/health`, and does no authentication: publish it only where you
want it reachable, or keep the Docker port mapping off and probe from
inside the container.

---

## 7. AFK Inactivity Timeout (`afk_timeout`)

The server tracks input activity per client machine (analog sticks, button presses, weapon triggers, and aim angle adjustments).

If a player remains completely inactive during an active match:
- At `afk_timeout - 30` seconds: A private warning notice is sent directly to the player:
  `AFK Warning: You will be kicked in 30 seconds for inactivity`
- At `afk_timeout` seconds: The player is automatically disconnected and a public notice is broadcast:
  `PlayerName was kicked for inactivity (AFK)`

### Configuration

In `config.toml`:
```toml
[network]
afk_timeout = 180   # Inactivity limit in seconds (0 = disabled, default = 180)
```

Or via environment variable:
```bash
export HALO_NET_AFK_TIMEOUT=180
```

---

## 8. Escalating Progressive Bans (`escalating_bans`)

When `network.escalating_bans = true` (default), host bans issued via `operator.sh ban <name>` scale automatically based on prior infractions found in `bans.txt` for that IP and hardware ID:

- **Strike 1:** 1 hour ban (`expires=TIMESTAMP`)
- **Strike 2:** 24 hour ban
- **Strike 3:** 7 day ban
- **Strike 4+:** Permanent ban

Expired temporary bans are ignored automatically by the host upon connection and do not block players. Confirmed speed hack auto-bans (`cheaters.txt`) are always permanent regardless of strike count.

### Configuration

In `config.toml`:
```toml
[network]
escalating_bans = true   # Set to false for permanent bans on first infraction
```

Or via environment variable:
```bash
export HALO_NET_ESCALATING_BANS=true
```

---

## 9. Lobby Map Voting (`map_voting`)

When `network.map_voting = true`, the server presents a vote to all players in the pregame lobby during the start countdown:

1. The server broadcasts available candidates from the playlist:
   ```text
   Vote Next Map: [1] Blood Gulch (Slayer) [2] Chill Out (CTF) [3] Sidewinder (Infection) (Type 1-3 in chat)
   ```
2. Players vote simply by typing `1`, `2`, `3`, etc. in chat.
   - Voted numbers are intercepted by the server and acknowledged privately.
   - Each player machine holds only one vote (typing a new number switches their vote).
3. Right before the game begins, the server announces the winner:
   ```text
   Winning Map: [1] Blood Gulch (Slayer) with 4 votes!
   ```
   and immediately loads that selection.

### Configuration

In `config.toml`:
```toml
[network]
map_voting = true       # Enable lobby chat map voting (default: false)
map_vote_options = 3    # Number of candidates to present (2 to 5, default: 3)
```

Or via environment variables:
```bash
export HALO_NET_MAP_VOTING=true
export HALO_NET_MAP_VOTE_OPTIONS=3
```

```md
# Guía de Instalación: Raspberry Pi 3B / 4 / 5 (ARM64)

Esta guía explica cómo ejecutar el servidor dedicado 24/7 de Halo: Combat Evolved en placas **Raspberry Pi** de 64 bits (**Raspberry Pi 3 Model B, 3B+, 4, 400 y 5**) y servidores en la nube basados en arquitectura **ARM64 (AArch64)** como **Oracle Cloud Ampere A1** (Free Tier) y AWS Graviton.

---

## 1. Requisitos de Hardware y Sistema Operativo

| Componente | Requisito Mínimo (RPi 3B) | Recomendado (RPi 4 / 5) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Procesador** | Broadcom BCM2837 (Quad-Core Cortex-A53 @ 1.2 GHz) | Broadcom BCM2711 / BCM2712 |
| **Memoria RAM** | 1 GB LPDDR2 | 2 GB a 8 GB LPDDR4/5 |
| **Almacenamiento** | MicroSD Clase 10 / A1 (8 GB mínimo libre) | SSD USB 3.0 / NVMe Hat |
| **Sistema Operativo** | **Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit)** o Ubuntu Server ARM64 | **Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit)** |
| **Arquitectura Kernel** | `aarch64` (`uname -m` debe reportar `aarch64`) | `aarch64` |

> **IMPORTANTE:** El kernel y sistema operativo deben ser de **64 bits**. Si instalas Raspberry Pi OS de 32 bits (`armhf`), el binario nativo de 64 bits no podrá ejecutarse. Verifica tu arquitectura ejecutando:
> ```bash
> uname -m
> # Debe devolver: aarch64
> ```

---

## 2. Optimización para Raspberry Pi 3B (1 GB de RAM)

Dado que la Raspberry Pi 3B comparte su 1 GB de RAM entre el procesador y el chip de video VideoCore, es indispensable optimizar la memoria asignada al sistema:

### Reducir la memoria de la GPU (headless)
En un servidor sin monitor no necesitamos memoria de video:
1. Abre `/boot/firmware/config.txt` (o `/boot/config.txt` en versiones anteriores):
   ```bash
   sudo nano /boot/firmware/config.txt
   ```
2. Agrega o modifica la línea:
   ```ini
   gpu_mem=16
   ```
3. Guarda (`Ctrl+O`, `Enter`) y sal (`Ctrl+X`). Esto deja más de 950 MB libres para el sistema y el servidor de Halo.

### Habilitar Swap ZRAM (Recomendado)
Para evitar bloqueos por falta de memoria RAM durante picos de carga:
```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y zram-tools
echo -e "ALGO=lz4\nPERCENT=50" | sudo tee /etc/default/zramswap
sudo systemctl restart zramswap
```

---

## 3. Despliegue con Docker (Método Recomendado)

Docker descarga automáticamente la imagen compilada para `linux/arm64`.

### Paso 1: Instalar Docker en Raspberry Pi
```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
newgrp docker
```

### Paso 2: Crear el directorio y copiar mapas
```bash
mkdir -p ~/halo-server/maps
cd ~/halo-server

# Copia los mapas originales de tu disco (ui.map, beavercreek.map, etc.)
cp /ruta/a/tus/mapas/* maps/
```

### Paso 3: Descargar `docker-compose.yml` y arrancar
```bash
curl -fsSL -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoshRob297/halo-ce-server/main/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSL -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoshRob297/halo-ce-server/main/server/config.toml

# Iniciar servidor en segundo plano
docker compose up -d

# Ver registros
docker compose logs -f
```

---

## 4. Despliegue Bare-Metal (systemd nativo)

Si prefieres ejecutar el binario directamente sin Docker:

```bash
# 1. Crear usuario dedicado del sistema
sudo useradd -r -s /usr/sbin/nologin -d /opt/halo-server halo

# 2. Descargar e instalar el binario ARM64
sudo mkdir -p /opt/halo-server/maps /opt/halo-server/custom_maps
cd /tmp
curl -fsSL -O https://github.com/JoshRob297/halo-ce-server/releases/latest/download/halo-server-linux-arm64.tar.gz
sudo tar -xzf halo-server-linux-arm64.tar.gz -C /opt/halo-server/
sudo chmod +x /opt/halo-server/halo /opt/halo-server/scripts/operator.sh
sudo chown -R halo:halo /opt/halo-server

# 3. Copiar mapas
sudo cp /ruta/a/tus/mapas/* /opt/halo-server/maps/
sudo chown -R halo:halo /opt/halo-server/maps

# 4. Habilitar servicio systemd
sudo cp /opt/halo-server/deploy/halo-server.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now halo-server
sudo journalctl -u halo-server -f
```

## 5. Rendimiento Medido en Raspberry Pi 3B

| Métrica | Medición Típica |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Uso de RAM en reposo** | ~85 MB a 92 MB |
| **Uso de RAM en partida activa (8 jugadores)** | ~110 MB |
| **Uso de CPU (4 núcleos Cortex-A53)** | 2.5% a 6.0% |
| **Tickrate del servidor** | 30.0 Hz constantes |
| **Consumo eléctrico** | ~2.5 Watts a 3.8 Watts |

La Raspberry Pi 3B es capaz de mantener una rotación ininterrumpida 24/7 con soporte para chat público, rotación aleatoria, votación en lobby y panel web sin sufrir caídas de frames ni estrangulamiento térmico.
