`docs/roadmap.md`:

```md
# Operator Roadmap

What the engine already provides, what the first release ships, and what
comes next in order of impact.

---

## What the engine already has (no code needed)

These work today on a running server. They are gaps in documentation, not
in the code.

### Console commands (host only, in-game)

The in-game developer console routes everything through
`hs_compile_and_evaluate` (the original Xbox scripting engine). The port
adds three host-only commands with Tab name completion:

| Command | Effect |
| :--- | :--- |
| `kick <name>` | Drops the player's machine; all players notified; player may rejoin immediately. |
| `ban <name>` | Drops + writes `ip=` and `hwid=` to `bans.txt` and `cheaters.txt` beside `debug.txt`. Host refuses that IP/HWID on future joins while running. Remove the line to unban. |
| `votekick <name>` | Host initiates a vote (same as a player doing it from the scoreboard). |

Any Halo Script function the original Xbox build had is also available
(`game_won`, `player_enable_input`, etc.).

### Telnet console (scripted access, 127.0.0.1)

`debug.telnet_console = true` (default: `false`) opens a listener on
`127.0.0.1:2323` (port: `debug.telnet_console_port`). Everything sent to
it passes through the same `console_process_command` as the in-game
console: `kick`, `ban`, and all Halo Script. No password; local only.

This is the operator's interface today. A thin wrapper on stdin can forward
lines to it.

### Mute (host, in-game chat)

Type `/mute <name> [minutes]` or `/unmute <name>` as a chat line (host
only). Mutes text lines and voice for all machines. The scoreboard's
right-click also does this. Internally: `network_chat_host_mute()`.

### Text chat settings

`network.text_chat`:

| Value | Effect |
| :--- | :--- |
| `on` | Chat allowed, links refused. |
| `links` | Chat allowed with links. |
| `off` | Chat fully disabled. |

**Known gap**: chat is automatically off in publicly listed games
(`p2p_hosting_listed()` forces it off regardless of the setting). A
dedicated public server therefore has no text chat today. Fixing this
requires a one-line change in `chat_host_config_flags()`.

### Vote-kick (players)

Built into `network_votekick.c`. Players start a vote from the scoreboard
or with `votekick <name>` in their console. The host counts by real address
+ HWID; needs more than half the electorate and at least 2 votes.
`network.votekick_minutes` sets the play time required to start a vote
(default: 5). `network.votekick_ban_minutes` sets the in-memory ban after a
passed vote (default: 30; not written to `bans.txt`).

### Anti-cheat that runs today

| Protection | How it works |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Speed hack detection** | Host measures client tick rate vs its own clock every 2 s. >10% faster and >0.5 s ahead: predictions refused immediately. After 10 s sustained + stream confirmation: auto-kick, `cheaters.txt`, `bans.txt`. |
| **Position validation** | Impossible positions (outside map) and unauthorized teleports are corrected or rejected. Legitimate teleporters are validated against map flags. |
| **Damage range check** | Melee capped at 1.5 m; projectile damage beyond the tag's `maximum_range` is refused. |
| **Aim assist block** | `network.block_mouse_aim_assist = true` sends a policy to all clients. |
| **Corrupt datagrams** | Discarded by design; the engine never trusts malformed packets. |
| **Connection rate limit** | 6 new connections per minute per address at the server layer. |
| **Stream-only trust** | Votes and sensitive messages accepted only from the client's TCP stream, never from bare UDP datagrams. |
| **HWID sanitization** | Hardware IDs are stripped to hex before storage or comparison. |

### Voice chat

Works. `network.voice_*` settings control it. The host can mute a player's
voice for everyone (same call as text mute). Players can mute individual
machines locally from the scoreboard.

---

## Milestone 1: Operator console (stdin pipe to telnet)

**Status: Done (v1.1.0).** Telnet console verified on headless linux build and wrapper tooling shipped.

Implementation summary:
1. `scripts/operator.sh` created to interface with telnet on 127.0.0.1:2323 (`kick`, `ban`, `votekick`, `say`, `status`, `raw`). [Done]
2. Documented operator commands, Docker usage, bare-metal workflow, and ban/cheater formats in `docs/operator.md`. [Done]
3. Telnet console verified on headless linux host (`debug.telnet_console = true` / `HALO_TELNET_CONSOLE=1`). Commands like `kick <name>` execute cleanly via telnet socket. [Done]
4. Log parsing implemented for `operator.sh status` extracting map, players, and game state (`pregame`, `in_game`, `postgame`) from 5-second engine logs. [Done]
5. `say` wrapper stubbed with warning in `operator.sh`; native script hook planned for upstream chat integration. [In Progress / Upstream]

Verified: `printf "kick test\n" | socat -t 2 - TCP:127.0.0.1:2323` and `scripts/operator.sh status` tested against running server on cachy.

## Milestone 2: Text chat in public servers

Implemented:
1. `chat_host_config_flags()` updated in `network_chat.c` to allow chat when `network.public_chat` is enabled (`(!p2p_hosting_listed() || config_boolean("network.public_chat"))`).
2. `network.public_chat` setting added in `port_config.c` (default: `false`, environment: `HALO_NET_PUBLIC_CHAT`).

## Milestone 3: Server password (join gate)

**Status: Done (v1.3.0).** Completed in engine commit `e7172ac7edbb69dcae984f4757c2514930bebf9a`.

Implemented:
1. `network.server_password` setting added in `port_config.c` (default: `""`, environment: `HALO_NET_SERVER_PASSWORD`).
2. `network_test.c` updated during host setup to call `p2p_set_hosting_password(server_password && server_password[0] ? server_password : NULL)`.
3. When set, `p2p_lobby.c` seals the lobby invite token with Argon2id salted with the host's key, advertising `_listing_password` (`locked = 1`) in the public browser. Clients must unlock with the matching password to join.
4. Documented in `server/config.toml` and `docs/operator.md`.
5. Verified compilation with `ci_build.py linux debug` on cachy.

## Milestone 4: Anti-cheat audit and hardening

**Status: Done.** Comprehensive code audit completed and documented in [`docs/anticheat.md`](anticheat.md).

Audit findings across all evaluated vectors:
1. **Weapon reach & production damage**: Verified. The checks in `network_test.c` are test-harness only (`debug.network_test_shoot`), but production damage handling in `network_damage.c:2061-2295` performs strict server-side validation on every hit report (verifying recent weapon ownership `distributed_player_deals`, firing burst rate `distributed_report_paid`, reach distance `distributed_player_could_fire`, melee distance `distributed_player_was_near`, historical target window `distributed_target_seen`, and line-of-sight raycasts `distributed_report_line_of_sight`).
2. **Aimbot / no-recoil**: Recoil and spread are simulated server-side via weapon action inputs (`update_server_handle_distributed_input`). External aim assistance or memory modification in client process memory remains undetectable server-side.
3. **Grenade count & ammunition**: Verified. Inventories, carried weapons, total ammo, and grenades are 100% authoritative on the host (`network_objects.c:1602-1634`). Clients never send inventory or ammo counts to the host; they only receive host states (`network_objects.c:3008-3058`).
4. **Scoreboard manipulation**: Verified. Kills, deaths, and team scores are calculated strictly from host simulation (`network_damage.c`, `network_distributed.c:3340-3423`). Clients cannot alter scores.
5. **HWID spoofing limit**: Verified. HWID and IP are matched against `bans.txt` on connection. Spoofed HWIDs cannot grant elevated privileges or duplicate votes (`network_votekick.c`).
6. Comprehensive operator guide and protection matrix written to `docs/anticheat.md`.

No engine vulnerabilities warranting micro-patches were identified; server authority is already strictly enforced by the netcode architecture.

---

## Known Gaps

The following engine-level limitations and threat vectors are unmitigated or require external controls:

| Vector | Severity | Status / Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Client Memory ESP / Aimbot** | **High** | Client execution space is unverified. Players modifying client memory to snap aim or draw player bounding boxes through walls cannot be prevented server-side. Mitigated by player vote-kicks and operator bans. |
| **HWID Spoofing** | **Medium** | Client hardware IDs (`p2p_hardware_id`) derive from local OS identifiers (`/etc/machine-id`, SMBIOS). Root/admin users can spoof them. Mitigated by IP banning and server join passwords (`network.server_password`). |
| **Unverified Speed Hack on UDP** | **Low** | If clock skew is detected solely on UDP datagrams without stream confirmation, the host logs to `cheaters.txt` as unverified but does not kick to protect against source IP spoofing. |

---

## Milestone 5: Health check endpoint

**Status: Done.** Completed in engine commits `2280e45b` (the endpoint) and
`e6d69b01` (the stop race and HEAD).

Implemented:
1. Native `server_health.{c,h}` module built into the engine running an independent `SDL_Thread` listening on 0.0.0.0 on TCP port `network.health_port` (`HALO_NET_HEALTH_PORT`).
2. Publishes snapshot every frame without locking the game loop, protected by `SDL_Mutex`.
3. Handles `GET /health` with HTTP 200 JSON payload:
   ```json
   {"status":"ok","state":"pregame","map":"bloodgulch","variant":"slayer","players":1,"max_players":128,"minutes_left":0,"listed":true,"uptime_seconds":17}
   ```
4. Returns HTTP 404 for any other request path.
5. Config setting added in `port_config.c` (default `0`: disabled) and documented in `port/linux/README.md`, `server/config.toml`, `docs/operator.md`, and `docker-compose.yml`.
6. Smoke tested on headless host cachy:
   - `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8099/health` -> `{"status":"ok","state":"pregame","map":"bloodgulch","variant":"slayer","players":1,"max_players":128,"minutes_left":0,"listed":true,"uptime_seconds":17}`
   - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8099/nope` -> `404`

## Milestone 8: Role-based access control (RBAC), user authentication & Web Login

**Status: Planned.** Native authentication system and tiered role permissions for server operations, in-game moderation, and Web Dashboard access.

Goals:
1. **Multi-Tiered Roles:**
   - **Owner:** Full system authority, configuration updates, role delegation, server shutdown/restart.
   - **Admin:** Playlist and map management (`Play Now`, rotation reordering), permanent bans, unbans, RCON access.
   - **Moderator:** Player kicks, temporary strikes/bans (up to 7 days), text chat muting, in-game warning broadcasts.
   - **Viewer:** Read-only access to live telemetry, player graphs, and scoreboard facts without administrative capabilities.
2. **Web Portal Authentication & Login:**
   - Session-based authentication via Argon2id hashed passwords (`server.web_password` and `server.web_moderator_password`).
   - Secure HttpOnly session cookies with automatic 12-hour expiration (or 30 minutes idle timeout) and CSRF protection.
   - Login interface displayed directly in the embedded Web Dashboard before granting access to sensitive controls (`/api/command`, `/api/rotation/next`, moderation actions).
3. **Audit Trail:**
   - Append-only logging of moderation actions to `control_audit.log` (timestamp, actor, target player, action taken, and reason).

# Guía del Dashboard Web y API REST

El Servidor Dedicado de Halo CE incluye un portal web de administración embebido en C sin dependencias externas. Se ejecuta directamente desde el binario del juego mediante HTTP estándar, sin requerir Node.js, Python, PHP ni servidores web externos (Nginx/Apache).

---

## 1. Arquitectura y Características

- **Puerto:** Configurado con `network.health_port` (por defecto: `8080`).
- **100% Opcional:** Fijar `network.health_port = 0` en `config.toml` desactiva por completo el socket HTTP con impacto cero en el rendimiento.
- **Frontend Ligero:** HTML5 semántico, CSS3 moderno (tema oscuro y diseño adaptativo) y JavaScript nativo puro sin librerías ni CDNs externos.
- **Assets Embebidos:** Todos los archivos de interfaz (`index.html`, `app.css`, `app.js`, `icon.svg`) están compilados en la memoria del ejecutable como matrices constantes.
- **Seguridad en Concurrencia:** El despachador HTTP corre en un hilo independiente POSIX (`server_health.c`). Las lecturas de telemetría obtienen un snapshot protegido por mutex para no retrasar el ciclo de juego de 30 Hz.

---

## 2. Módulos y Pestañas del Dashboard

### 1. Pestaña Status (`/`)
<p align="center">
  <img src="screenshots/dashboard_status.png" alt="Dashboard Status" width="800">
</p>

Telemetría en tiempo real actualizada cada 2 segundos por sondeo activo:
- **Telemetría del Servidor:** Tiempo de actividad (uptime), jugadores conectados, capacidad máxima, tickrate y consumo de memoria.
- **Estado de Partida:** Mapa en curso, título de misión, modo de juego activo y tiempo transcurrido.
- **Marcador en Vivo:** Bajas (kills), muertes, puntuación individual, ping y equipo de cada jugador.
- **Gráfica Histórica de Jugadores:** Gráfica interactiva SVG con la fluctuación de jugadores durante los últimos 10 minutos.

### 2. Pestaña Rotation (`#rotation`)
<p align="center">
  <img src="screenshots/dashboard_rotation.png" alt="Gestor de Rotación" width="450">
</p>

Administración completa de la lista de reproducción:
- **Lista Activa:** Visualiza la secuencia programada con botones de reordenamiento (`Up`, `Down`, `Remove`).
- **Salto Inmediato (`Play Now`):** Cambia inmediatamente la partida en curso al mapa y modo seleccionado sin reiniciar el servidor.
- **Agregar Combinación:** Selector interactivo que incluye:
  - Los 13 mapas multijugador clásicos (`beavercreek`, `bloodgulch`, `wizard`, etc.).
  - Las 10 misiones de campaña cooperativa (`a10` Pillar of Autumn hasta `d40` The Maw).
  - Todos los modos de juego estándar y custom (`slayer`, `ctf`, `oddball`, `king`, `race`, `swat`, `infection`, `gun_game`, `hardcore_*` y `coop`).

<p align="center">

Editor visual de variables de configuración con guardado en caliente:
- `network.server_name`: Nombre visible en el buscador público oficial.
- `network.tunnel_port`: Puerto UDP de juego (por defecto: 2302).
- `network.map_rotation`: Orden de reproducción (`sequence` o `shuffle`).
- `network.map_voting`: Votación por chat en el lobby.
- `network.afk_timeout`: Tiempo de inactividad antes de auto-kick en segundos.
- `network.map_share` y `network.map_share_upload`: Distribución P2P BitTorrent de mapas custom y límite de subida en KB/s.
- `network.coop_enemies_mode` y `network.coop_pickups`: Algoritmos de escalado en campaña (`per_player`, `none`, `multiplier`).
- `bots.count`: Cantidad de bots IA multijugador activos (0 a 16).

### 4. Consola Web / RCON Interactiva (`#console`)
Terminal interactiva conectada al compilador Halo Script y despachador de comandos del motor. Permite ejecutar cualquier instrucción soportada por `operator.sh` (`status`, `kick <jugador>`, `ban <jugador>`, `sv_map`, etc.).

## 3. Especificación de la API REST

Todos los endpoints devuelven respuestas en formato JSON con el campo `"ok": true|false`.

### `GET /api/status`
Devuelve el estado completo del servidor, telemetría y marcador en vivo.

### `GET /api/maps`
Lista todos los mapas multijugador y niveles de campaña soportados.

### `GET /api/gametypes`
Lista las variantes de juego integradas y el modo `coop`.

### `GET /api/settings`
Devuelve el arreglo de parámetros tipados con valores actuales, tipos de dato y opciones válidas.

### `POST /api/rotation/next`
Avanza de inmediato a la siguiente partida programada en la rotación.

### `POST /api/command`
Ejecuta un comando de consola o expresión de Halo Script.

**Cuerpo de la Petición:**
```json
{
  "line": "kick \"Griefer\""
}
```

## 4. Configuración de Red y Seguridad

1. **Acceso Local y en LAN:**
   - En despliegues bare-metal, abre el puerto TCP `8080` en tu firewall:
     ```bash
     # UFW (Ubuntu / Debian)
     sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp
     ```
2. **Proxy Inverso con HTTPS (Recomendado para Internet Público):**
   - Para exponer el dashboard fuera de la red local, se recomienda utilizar Nginx o Caddy como proxy inverso con certificado SSL y autenticación HTTP básica (Basic Auth):
   ```nginx
   server {
       listen 443 ssl http2;
       server_name halo-admin.tudominio.com;

       ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/tudominio.com/fullchain.pem;
       ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/tudominio.com/privkey.pem;

       auth_basic "Acceso Restringido";
       auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd;

       location / {
           proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
           proxy_set_header Host $host;
           proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
       }
   }
   ```

`docs/web-dashboard.md`:

```md
# Web Dashboard & REST API Guide

The Halo CE Dedicated Server embeds a zero-dependency, low-latency web management portal directly compiled into the C binary. It operates over standard HTTP without requiring Node.js, Python, PHP, or external web servers (Nginx/Apache).

---

## 1. Overview & Architecture

- **Port:** Configured via `network.health_port` (default: `8080`).
- **Fully Optional:** Setting `network.health_port = 0` in `config.toml` disables the HTTP listener completely with zero performance impact.
- **Frontend Stack:** Vanilla HTML5, modern CSS3 (responsive grid and dark theme), and pure ECMAScript (no npm or external CDN dependencies).
- **Embedded Assets:** All frontend files (`index.html`, `app.css`, `app.js`, `icon.svg`) are baked into the binary as read-only memory arrays.
- **Concurrency & Safety:** The HTTP dispatcher runs on an independent POSIX background thread (`server_health.c`). Telemetry reads acquire an internal mutex snapshot to avoid stalling the 30 Hz game tick loop.

---

## 2. Dashboard Modules & Tabs

### 1. Status Tab (`/`)
<p align="center">
  <img src="screenshots/dashboard_status.png" alt="Status Dashboard" width="800">
</p>

Provides real-time telemetry updated every 2 seconds via live polling:
- **Server Health Facts:** Server uptime, active player count, maximum capacity, tickrate, memory consumption, and host link status.
- **Current Game State:** Active map name, mission title, gametype ruleset, and match elapsed time.
- **Live Scoreboard:** Real-time kill count, deaths, scores, ping, and team assignments for all connected players.
- **Player History Graph:** Interactive SVG timeline tracking connected player density over the trailing 10 minutes.

### 2. Rotation Tab (`#rotation`)
<p align="center">
  <img src="screenshots/dashboard_rotation.png" alt="Rotation Manager" width="450">
</p>

Allows full control over the map and gametype playlist cycle:
- **Active Playlist:** Displays the planned match sequence with reordering controls (`Up`, `Down`, `Remove`).
- **Instant Skip / Switch (`Play Now`):** Immediately advances the server to the selected map/mode combination without restarting the daemon.
- **Add Combination:** Interactive dropdown selector listing:
  - All 13 multiplayer maps (`beavercreek`, `bloodgulch`, `wizard`, etc.).
  - All 10 campaign co-op missions (`a10` Pillar of Autumn through `d40` The Maw).
  - All standard and custom gametypes (`slayer`, `ctf`, `oddball`, `king`, `race`, `swat`, `infection`, `gun_game`, `hardcore_*`, and `coop`).

### 3. Settings Tab (`#settings`)
<p align="center">
  <img src="screenshots/dashboard_settings.png" alt="Settings Editor" width="450">
</p>

Visual configuration editor mapping directly to parameters:
- `network.server_name`: Server title displayed in the Master Browser.
- `network.tunnel_port`: Primary UDP game listening port (default: 2302).
- `network.map_rotation`: Mode sequence order (`sequence` or `shuffle`).
- `network.map_voting`: In-lobby chat voting toggle.
- `network.afk_timeout`: Automatic idle kick timer in seconds.
- `network.map_share` & `network.map_share_upload`: BitTorrent P2P map distribution toggles and bandwidth rate limiter.
- `network.coop_enemies_mode` & `network.coop_pickups`: Campaign co-op scaling algorithms (`per_player`, `none`, `multiplier`).
- `bots.count`: Number of active AI multiplayer bots (0 to 16).

### 4. Interactive Web Console / RCON (`#console`)
A browser-based terminal connected directly to the engine's Halo Script compiler and command parser. Supports executing any command supported by `operator.sh` or the internal telnet interface (`help`, `status`, `sv_map`, `kick <player>`, `ban <player>`, etc.).

---

## 3. REST API Specification

All endpoints return JSON responses with an `"ok": true|false` status field.

### `GET /api/status`
Returns comprehensive live server state and scoreboard facts.

**Sample Response:**
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "name": "JOCES 24/7 CUSTOM",
  "state": "ingame",
  "map": "beavercreek",
  "title": "Battle Creek",
  "gametype": "gun_game",
  "time": "04:32",
  "time_limit": 15,
  "players": 4,
  "max_players": 16,
  "history": [0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4],
  "scoreboard": [
    {"index": 0, "name": "MasterChief", "team": 0, "score": 12, "kills": 12, "deaths": 4, "ping": 18},
    {"index": 1, "name": "Arbiter", "team": 1, "score": 9, "kills": 9, "deaths": 6, "ping": 25}
  ]
}
```

### `GET /api/maps`
Lists all available multiplayer and campaign levels supported by the server engine.

### `GET /api/gametypes`
Lists all built-in multiplayer variants (`slayer`, `swat`, `infection`, `gun_game`, etc.) and campaign `coop`.

### `GET /api/settings`
Returns an array of typed configuration parameters with metadata, current values, types, and allowed options.

### `POST /api/rotation/next`
Advances the server to the next scheduled match in the playlist.

### `POST /api/command`
Executes a console command or Halo Script expression.

**Request Payload:**
```json
{
  "line": "kick \"Griefer\""
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "lines": ["player Griefer kicked"]
}
```

---

## 4. Security & Network Configuration

1. **Local Access vs LAN Access:**
   - In standard bare-metal deployments, ensure port `8080` (TCP) is allowed through `nftables`, `ufw`, or `firewalld`:
     ```bash
     sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp
     ```
2. **Reverse Proxy & HTTPS (Recommended for Public Internet Access):**
   - For secure remote access across public networks, place the dashboard behind an Nginx or Caddy reverse proxy with SSL termination and basic authentication:
   ```nginx
   server {
       listen 443 ssl http2;
       server_name halo-admin.example.com;

       ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
       ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

       auth_basic "Restricted Access";
       auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd;

       location / {
           proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
           proxy_set_header Host $host;
           proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
       }
   }
   ```

`docs/windows.md`:

```md
# Windows Headless Dedicated Server Guide

This guide covers running the Halo CE (OpenCE) dedicated server headless on Windows without a display, GPU, or sound hardware.

---

## 1. What Is Verified vs Not Verified

- **Verified in CI (`windows-2025`):** The Windows binary (`halo.exe`) successfully initialises SDL headless using dummy drivers (`SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy`), parses headless launch arguments, and proceeds through engine startup to the game data verification phase.
- **Not Verified in CI:** A full multi-player hosted network game is not simulated in CI because retail game maps cannot be redistributed or embedded into CI pipelines. Running full game sessions requires valid retail Xbox map files provided by the operator.

---

## 2. Obtaining Game Maps on Windows

The dedicated server requires the Xbox map files (`*.map`) extracted from a legally owned retail disc of *Halo: Combat Evolved* (Xbox).

1. **Extracting from Disc Image (ISO):**
   - Use `extract-xiso` or 7-Zip to extract the contents of your Xbox ISO.
   - Locate the `maps/` directory inside the disc image.
2. **Directory Structure:**
   Place the maps in a `maps/` folder beside `halo.exe`:
   ```text
   C:\halo\
   ├── halo.exe
   ├── SDL3.dll
   ├── config.toml
   └── maps\
       ├── ui.map
       ├── bloodgulch.map
       ├── bitmaps.map
       ├── sounds.map
       └── ...
   ```
   If Custom Edition maps are used, place them inside a `custom_maps\` folder beside `maps\`:
   ```text
   C:\halo\
   └── custom_maps\
       ├── cbeaver.map
       └── ...
   ```
   If maps reside in another location, set `paths.data` in `config.toml` to the directory containing `maps\`.

---

## 3. Running Headless by Hand

### Command Prompt (`cmd.exe`)

Open Command Prompt, set the environment variables, and start `halo.exe`:

```cmd
cd /d C:\halo
set SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy
set SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy
set HALO_NETWORK_TEST=host:bloodgulch:slayer
set HALO_EXIT_AFTER=0
halo.exe
```

### PowerShell

Open PowerShell, set the process-level environment variables, and start `halo.exe`:

```powershell
Set-Location "C:\halo"
$env:SDL_VIDEODRIVER = "dummy"
$env:SDL_AUDIODRIVER = "dummy"
$env:HALO_NETWORK_TEST = "host:bloodgulch:slayer"
$env:HALO_EXIT_AFTER = "0"
.\halo.exe
```

---

## 4. Configuration (`config.toml`)

When `halo.exe` runs for the first time, it writes default settings to `config.toml` in its working directory. Key settings for headless operation:

```toml
[paths]
# If your maps are not in C:\halo\maps, point to the folder containing maps/
data = "C:\\halo"

[network]
online = true
host_public = true
# Optional password gate
server_password = ""
# Optional health monitor port (0 = disabled)
health_port = 8099

[debug]
# Telnet operator console (local loopback)
telnet_console = true
telnet_console_port = 2323
```

---

## 5. Windows Firewall Rule

Allow inbound UDP traffic on port 2302 so clients can discover and join the server. Run in an elevated PowerShell prompt:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Halo CE Server" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 2302 -Action Allow
```

If the health check endpoint is enabled and needs external access, create an inbound rule for TCP 8099:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Halo CE Health" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8099 -Action Allow
```

---

## 6. Running as a Windows Service with NSSM

To ensure the server runs continuously in the background and restarts automatically on failure or reboot, use the Non-Sucking Service Manager ([NSSM](https://nssm.cc/)).

> **Note:** The NSSM configuration below is documented according to standard Windows service specifications; it has not been directly exercised on bare-metal Windows test rigs by our automated CI.

Run the following commands from an elevated Command Prompt:

```cmd
nssm install HaloServer "C:\halo\halo.exe"
nssm set HaloServer AppDirectory "C:\halo"
nssm set HaloServer AppEnvironmentExtra SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy
nssm set HaloServer AppStdout "C:\halo\server.log"
nssm set HaloServer AppStderr "C:\halo\server.err.log"
nssm set HaloServer AppStopMethodSkip 6
nssm set HaloServer AppExit Default Restart
nssm start HaloServer
```

### Understanding `AppStopMethodSkip 6`

The Halo engine loop does not process standard window closure messages (`WM_CLOSE`) or console control events (`SIGTERM` equivalents) during headless operation. Setting `AppStopMethodSkip 6` instructs NSSM to skip `WM_CLOSE` and console events, ensuring NSSM can cleanly terminate and restart the process via hard process termination when stopping or cycling the service.

Service management commands:
```cmd
nssm status HaloServer
nssm stop HaloServer
nssm restart HaloServer
nssm remove HaloServer confirm
```

---

## 7. Operator Console on Windows

The dedicated server includes an unauthenticated telnet administration console bound to `127.0.0.1:2323` when `debug.telnet_console = true`.

To connect from Windows:

### Using PowerShell or Netcat (`nc`)
PowerShell test connection:
```powershell
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 127.0.0.1 -Port 2323
```

If `nc` (netcat) or PuTTY is installed:
```cmd
nc 127.0.0.1 2323
```

Commands supported over the telnet console:
- `kick <name>`: Disconnect a player.
- `ban <name>`: Disconnect a player and write IP/HWID to `bans.txt` and `cheaters.txt`.
- `votekick <name>`: Initiate a vote kick.
- Halo Script engine commands (`game_won`, etc.).

For complete operator documentation, see [docs/operator.md](operator.md).

---

## 8. Health Endpoint on Windows

If `network.health_port` is configured (e.g. `8099`), the server serves HTTP status snapshots. Windows 10+ includes `curl.exe` out of the box:

```cmd
curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8099/health
```

Expected output:
```json
{"status":"ok","state":"pregame","map":"bloodgulch","variant":"slayer","players":1,"max_players":128,"minutes_left":0,"listed":true,"uptime_seconds":42}
```

Probe with `HEAD` for lightweight uptime monitors:
```cmd
curl.exe -I http://127.0.0.1:8099/health
```

`scripts/halo-update.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# halo-update.sh: Actualizador atomico y seguro para Halo CE Dedicated Server
#
# Uso:
#   sudo ./scripts/halo-update.sh [/srv/halo] [--check]
#
# Principios de Seguridad:
#   1. Verificacion de Checksum SHA-256 oficial antes de reemplazar archivos.
#   2. Backup automatico de la version previa para rollback inmediato si falla el arranque.
#   3. Reemplazo atomico (mv) para evitar corrupcion de binarios en disco.
#   4. Preservacion absoluta de config.toml, maps/ y partidas guardadas.
#   5. Smoke-test automatico tras la actualizacion con rollback si falla.
set -euo pipefail

DIR="${1:-/srv/halo}"
CHECK_ONLY=false
if [ "${2:-}" = "--check" ]; then
    CHECK_ONLY=true
fi

REPO="JoshRob297/halo-ce-server"
API_URL="https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}/releases/latest"

echo "=== Verificador de Actualizaciones de Halo CE Server ==="
echo "Directorio de instalacion: $DIR"

command -v curl >/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: falta curl" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v sha256sum >/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: falta sha256sum" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v tar >/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: falta tar" >&2; exit 1; }

# Detectar arquitectura del sistema
ARCH=$(uname -m)
case "$ARCH" in
    x86_64)
        ASSET="halo-server-linux-x64.tar.gz"
        ;;
    aarch64|arm64)
        ASSET="halo-server-linux-arm64.tar.gz"
        ;;
    i386|i686)
        ASSET="halo-server-linux-x86.tar.gz"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Arquitectura no reconocida ($ARCH), usando paquete portable universal"
        ASSET="halo-linux-portable.tar.gz"
        ;;
esac

echo "Arquitectura detectada: $ARCH -> Paquete: $ASSET"

# Consultar ultima release
RELEASE_JSON=$(curl -fsSL "$API_URL" || { echo "ERROR: no se pudo consultar la API de GitHub" >&2; exit 1; })
LATEST_TAG=$(echo "$RELEASE_JSON" | grep -m1 '"tag_name":' | cut -d '"' -f 4)

# Comprobar version local
LOCAL_VERSION="desconocida"
if [ -f "$DIR/.version" ]; then
    LOCAL_VERSION=$(cat "$DIR/.version")
fi

echo "Version instalada: $LOCAL_VERSION"
echo "Ultima version:    $LATEST_TAG"

if [ "$LOCAL_VERSION" = "$LATEST_TAG" ]; then
    echo "El servidor ya se encuentra en la version mas reciente ($LATEST_TAG)."
    exit 0
fi

if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" = true ]; then
    echo "Nueva version disponible: $LATEST_TAG"
    exit 0
fi

if [ "$(id -u)" != "0" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: la actualizacion requiere permisos de root (ejecuta con sudo)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/download/${LATEST_TAG}/${ASSET}"
CHECKSUM_URL="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/download/${LATEST_TAG}/SHA256SUMS"

TMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/halo-update-XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT

echo "Descargando release $LATEST_TAG..."
curl -fsSL "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o "$TMP_DIR/$ASSET"
curl -fsSL "$CHECKSUM_URL" -o "$TMP_DIR/SHA256SUMS"

echo "Verificando integridad criptografica SHA-256..."
cd "$TMP_DIR"
EXPECTED_HASH=$(grep "$ASSET" SHA256SUMS | awk '{print $1}')
ACTUAL_HASH=$(sha256sum "$ASSET" | awk '{print $1}')

if [ -n "$EXPECTED_HASH" ] && [ "$EXPECTED_HASH" != "$ACTUAL_HASH" ]; then
    echo "ERROR CRITICO: Checksum SHA-256 no coincide!" >&2
    echo "Esperado: $EXPECTED_HASH" >&2
    echo "Obtenido: $ACTUAL_HASH" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "Checksum verificado correctamente (SHA-256 OK)."

echo "Descomprimiendo archivos..."
mkdir -p "$TMP_DIR/unpacked"
tar -xzf "$ASSET" -C "$TMP_DIR/unpacked"

# Localizar el binario descomprimido
EXTRACTED_DIR="$TMP_DIR/unpacked"
if [ -d "$TMP_DIR/unpacked/${ASSET%.tar.gz}" ]; then
    EXTRACTED_DIR="$TMP_DIR/unpacked/${ASSET%.tar.gz}"
fi

if [ ! -f "$EXTRACTED_DIR/halo" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: el paquete no contiene el binario 'halo'" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Detener servicio si esta corriendo
SERVICE_WAS_ACTIVE=false
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet halo-server; then
    echo "Deteniendo halo-server temporalmente para actualizacion atomica..."
    systemctl stop halo-server
    SERVICE_WAS_ACTIVE=true
fi

# Crear backup de la version previa
BACKUP_DIR="$DIR/backup-pre-update"
rm -rf "$BACKUP_DIR"
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
if [ -f "$DIR/halo" ]; then
    cp -p "$DIR/halo" "$BACKUP_DIR/"
fi
if [ -f "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0" ]; then
    cp -p "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0" "$BACKUP_DIR/"
fi

echo "Aplicando actualizacion atomica..."
cp -p "$EXTRACTED_DIR/halo" "$DIR/halo.new"
chmod 755 "$DIR/halo.new"
mv -f "$DIR/halo.new" "$DIR/halo"

if [ -f "$EXTRACTED_DIR/libSDL3.so.0" ]; then
    cp -p "$EXTRACTED_DIR/libSDL3.so.0" "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0.new"
    chmod 755 "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0.new"
    mv -f "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0.new" "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0"
fi

if [ -d "$EXTRACTED_DIR/scripts" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$DIR/scripts"
    cp -rp "$EXTRACTED_DIR/scripts/"* "$DIR/scripts/"
fi

# Guardar version actualizada
echo "$LATEST_TAG" > "$DIR/.version"

# Ajustar permisos para el usuario del servicio
if id -u halo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R halo:halo "$DIR/halo" "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0" "$DIR/scripts" "$DIR/.version" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Smoke-test de arranque
echo "Ejecutando smoke test de arranque..."
if SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy timeout 2 "$DIR/halo" --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ $? -eq 124 ]; then
    echo "Smoke test superado con exito."
else
    echo "ALERTA: El nuevo binario fallo el smoke-test. Iniciando rollback de seguridad..."
    if [ -f "$BACKUP_DIR/halo" ]; then
        mv -f "$BACKUP_DIR/halo" "$DIR/halo"
    fi
    if [ -f "$BACKUP_DIR/libSDL3.so.0" ]; then
        mv -f "$BACKUP_DIR/libSDL3.so.0" "$DIR/libSDL3.so.0"
    fi
    if [ "$SERVICE_WAS_ACTIVE" = true ]; then
        systemctl start halo-server
    fi
    echo "Rollback completado. El servidor se mantiene en su version previa funcional."
    exit 1
fi

# Reanudar servicio
if [ "$SERVICE_WAS_ACTIVE" = true ]; then
    echo "Reanudando halo-server..."
    systemctl start halo-server
fi

echo "Actualizacion a $LATEST_TAG completada exitosamente!"

```

`scripts/install-baremetal.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install-baremetal.sh: baja el server de la release y deja el servicio listo.
#
#   sudo ./scripts/install-baremetal.sh [/srv/halo] [URL del binario]
#
# El primer argumento es el directorio de instalacion (default /srv/halo).
# El segundo es la URL del binario de la release; por default la ultima
# release de este repositorio (server-linux-x86-portable.tar.gz -> halo).
#
# No trae mapas: copialos despues a <dir>/maps/ desde tu disco.
set -euo pipefail

DIR="${1:-/srv/halo}"
BIN_URL="${2:-https://github.com/JoshRob297/halo-ce-server/releases/latest/download/halo-linux-portable.tar.gz}"

if [ "$(id -u)" != "0" ]; then
    echo "correlo como root (usa sudo)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

command -v curl >/dev/null || { echo "falta curl" >&2; exit 1; }

echo "instalando en $DIR"

# el usuario del servicio, con home dentro del dir (partidas guardadas)
id -u halo >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd --system --home-dir "$DIR/home" --create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin halo

mkdir -p "$DIR/maps" "$DIR/custom_maps"
cd "$DIR"

echo "bajando $BIN_URL"
curl -fsSL "$BIN_URL" -o halo.tar.gz
tar -xzf halo.tar.gz
rm halo.tar.gz
[ -x "$DIR/halo" ] || { echo "el tarball no trajo $DIR/halo" >&2; exit 1; }

# la config de ejemplo, si no hay una
if [ ! -f "$DIR/config.toml" ]; then
    cp /usr/share/halo-ce-server/config.toml "$DIR/config.toml" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

chown -R halo:halo "$DIR"

# la unidad de systemd (la copia embebida, o la del repo)
UNIT_SRC="$(dirname "$0")/../systemd/halo-server.service"
if [ -f "$UNIT_SRC" ]; then
    sed "s|/srv/halo|$DIR|g" "$UNIT_SRC" > /etc/systemd/system/halo-server.service
else
    sed "s|/srv/halo|$DIR|g" "$DIR/halo-server.service" > /etc/systemd/system/halo-server.service
fi

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now halo-server

echo
echo "listo. Arrancalo con: systemctl restart halo-server"
echo "log:               journalctl -u halo-server -f"
echo "mapas:             $DIR/maps/"
echo "config:            $DIR/config.toml"

```

`scripts/operator.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

HOST="${HALO_CONSOLE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
PORT="${HALO_CONSOLE_PORT:-2323}"
LOG_FILE="${HALO_LOG_FILE:-/root/.local/share/halo-linux/debug.txt}"

usage() {
    cat << 'EOF'
Usage:
  operator.sh kick <name>       # sends: kick <name>
  operator.sh ban <name>        # sends: ban <name>
  operator.sh votekick <name>   # sends: votekick <name>
  operator.sh say <text>        # logs warning (say not yet implemented natively)
  operator.sh status            # reads from server log and prints parsed state
  operator.sh raw <command>     # sends raw command to telnet console
EOF
    exit 1
}

send_command() {
    cmd="$1"
    if command -v socat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf "%s\n" "$cmd" | socat -t 2 - "TCP:${HOST}:${PORT}" 2>/dev/null || {
            echo "Error: failed to connect to console at ${HOST}:${PORT}" >&2
            exit 1
        }
    elif command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if nc -h 2>&1 | grep -q -- "-q"; then
            printf "%s\n" "$cmd" | nc -w 2 -q 1 "$HOST" "$PORT" 2>/dev/null || {
                echo "Error: failed to connect to console at ${HOST}:${PORT}" >&2
                exit 1
            }
        else
            printf "%s\n" "$cmd" | nc -w 2 "$HOST" "$PORT" 2>/dev/null || {
                echo "Error: failed to connect to console at ${HOST}:${PORT}" >&2
                exit 1
            }
        fi
    else
        echo "Error: neither socat nor nc found" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

cmd="${1:-}"
case "$cmd" in
    kick)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage
        shift
        send_command "kick $*"
        ;;
    ban)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage
        shift
        send_command "ban $*"
        ;;
    votekick)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage
        shift
        send_command "votekick $*"
        ;;
    say)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage
        shift
        echo "Warning: say is not yet implemented natively by the dedicated server" >&2
        ;;
    raw)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage
        shift
        send_command "$*"
        ;;
    status)
        if [ ! -f "$LOG_FILE" ]; then
            echo "Error: log file not found at $LOG_FILE" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        # Log format examples:
        #   halo-linux: network test: game 1, slayer on bloodgulch
        #   halo-linux: server: state 1 ..., map levels\test\bloodgulch\bloodgulch, 600 seconds left, 3 players of 16
        game_line=$(grep "network test: game\|network test: hosting" "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 || true)
        state_line=$(grep "server: state" "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 || true)

        if [ -z "$game_line" ] && [ -z "$state_line" ]; then
            echo "Error: no server state found in log at $LOG_FILE" >&2
            exit 1
        fi

        # Extract variant and map from "game N, variant on map" line
        if [ -n "$game_line" ]; then
            variant=$(printf '%s\n' "$game_line" | sed -n 's/.*network test: game [0-9]*, \([^ ]*\) on .*/\1/p')
            map_name=$(printf '%s\n' "$game_line" | sed -n 's/.*network test: game [0-9]*, [^ ]* on \(.*\)/\1/p' | tr -d '\r')
            if [ -z "$map_name" ]; then
                # hosting line: "network test: hosting bloodgulch"
                map_name=$(printf '%s\n' "$game_line" | sed -n 's/.*network test: hosting \(.*\)/\1/p' | tr -d '\r')
                variant="lobby"
            fi
        fi

        # Extract state and players from "server: state N" line
        if [ -n "$state_line" ]; then
            raw_state=$(printf '%s\n' "$state_line" | sed -n 's/.*server: state \([0-9]\).*/\1/p')
            raw_players=$(printf '%s\n' "$state_line" | sed -n 's/.*, \([0-9]*\) players of.*/\1/p')
            case "$raw_state" in
                0) state="pregame" ;;
                1) state="in_game" ;;
                2) state="postgame" ;;
                *) state="unknown" ;;
            esac
            players="${raw_players:-0}"
        else
            state="starting"
            players="0"
        fi

        printf "map: %s | variant: %s | players: %s | state: %s\n" \
            "${map_name:-unknown}" "${variant:-unknown}" "$players" "$state"
        ;;
    *)
        usage
        ;;
esac

```

`specs/multiarch-arm64/plan.md`:

```md
# Architecture Plan: Multi-Architecture Linux Builds (ARM64 / x86_64 / i686)

## Arquitectura Propuesta

```
                  [ Código Fuente C89 / OpenCE v38 ]
                                  |
              +-------------------+-------------------+
              |                                       |
     [ tools/linux_build.py ]                [ tools/lp64_build.py ]
              |                                       |
    [ Target: i686-linux-gnu ]              [ tools/lp64_rewrite.py ]
              |                        (Reescritura de tipos: long -> int)
              |                                       |
              |                        +--------------+--------------+
              |                        |                             |
              v                        v                             v
      [ halo-linux-x86 ]      [ halo-linux-x64 ]            [ halo-linux-arm64 ]
        (i686 32-bit)          (x86_64 64-bit)                (aarch64 64-bit)
              |                        |                             |
              +------------------------+-----------------------------+
                                       |
                        [ GitHub Actions CI Workflow ]
                                       |
                   +-------------------+-------------------+
                   |                                       |
      [ GitHub Releases Tarballs ]             [ Docker Buildx Hub / GHCR ]
    - halo-server-linux-x86.tar.gz            - linux/amd64 (x64)
    - halo-server-linux-x64.tar.gz            - linux/arm64 (Raspberry Pi 3B/4/5)
    - halo-server-linux-arm64.tar.gz
```

## Decisiones de Arquitectura

### Decisión 1: Estrategia de tipos en arquitecturas de 64 bits (LP64)
- **Contexto:** El código original de Xbox 2001 compila bajo MSVC donde `long` es de 32 bits. En Linux 64-bit (`LP64`), `long` es de 64 bits, lo que provocaría desalineación en structs de red y tags del mapa.
- **Decisión:** Adoptar la técnica de compilación de Chupathingy/OpenCE mediante `tools/lp64_rewrite.py` y `source/cseries/xbox_address.h` con el flag `-DHALO_64BIT=1`.
- **Alternativas descartadas:**
  - *Usar ILP32 en ARM (arm64_32 de Apple):* Requiere toolchains no estándar en Linux comunes y carece de soporte directo en distribuciones Debian/Ubuntu para Raspberry Pi.
  - *Box86 emulado:* Agrega sobrecarga y complejidad operativa al usuario; se descartó a favor del binario ELF nativo puro.
- **Consecuencias:** Se obtiene un binario ELF aarch64 nativo sin dependencias de emulación, con ejecución directa en cualquier distribución Linux ARM64 estándar.

### Decisión 2: Espacio de memoria y direcciones Xbox (`xbox_address.h` / `xbox_memory.c`)
- **Contexto:** Las etiquetas de mapas y el estado físico del juego esperan direcciones de 32 bits.
- **Decisión:** Para ARM64, ubicar la base de memoria Xbox en `XBOX_ADDRESS_SPACE_BASE = 0x4000000000ULL` (256 GB), dentro de los límites de los kernels ARM64 con espacio de direcciones de 39 bits (Raspberry Pi OS).
- **Consecuencias:** Cero colisiones de memoria en hosts con poca RAM (como el 1 GB de la RPi 3B).

### Decisión 3: Generación de binarios en CI
- **Contexto:** Raspberry Pi 3B tiene recursos limitados para compilar el proyecto directamente en la placa.
- **Decisión:** Utilizar Clang cross-compilation en GitHub Actions (`ubuntu-latest` x86_64) con sysroots ARM64 ligeros (`aarch64-linux-gnu`) y compilar los artefactos en la nube.
- **Consecuencias:** Compilaciones ultrarrápidas (< 5 minutos) y entrega directa de binarios precompilados en los releases.

## Riesgos y Mitigación
1. **Riesgo:** Desalineación de estructuras de red entre clientes v38 (32-bit) y el servidor (64-bit).
   - *Mitigación:* Tests de aserciones estáticas de tamaño de structs (`_Static_assert(sizeof(...) == ..., ...)`) antes de emitir paquetes.
2. **Riesgo:** Agotamiento de memoria RAM en RPi 3B (1 GB).
   - *Mitigación:* El servidor headless se compila sin SDL3 gráfico ni dependencias X11/Wayland, manteniendo el RSS por debajo de 100 MB.

## Niveles de Testing
1. **Unitario:** Test de compilación y enlace cruzado con `aarch64-linux-gnu`.
2. **Integración:** Ejecución en contenedor Docker ARM64 emulado por QEMU en el CI para validar que arranca, carga mapas y responde en el puerto 8080.
3. **Red:** Verificación de conexión de clientes v38 y respuesta del Web Dashboard.

```

`specs/multiarch-arm64/spec.md`:

```md
# Multi-Architecture Support: Linux ARM64 (Raspberry Pi 3B / Oracle Cloud) & x86_64

## Problema
El servidor dedicado de Halo CE actual (`halo-ce-server`) se compila exclusivamente como binario de 32 bits i686 (`--target=i686-linux-gnu`). Esto presenta dos limitaciones críticas:
1. En placas de desarrollo como **Raspberry Pi 3B / 4 / 5** y servidores cloud ARMv8 (Oracle Cloud Ampere A1, AWS Graviton), no se puede ejecutar de forma nativa sin recurrir a emuladores (como Box86).
2. En distribuciones Linux de 64 bits modernas (Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Alpine), requiere instalar paquetes multilib/i386 de 32 bits (`libc6:i386`), aumentando el tamaño y complejidad del despliegue Docker y bare-metal.

## Alcance
- Dentro:
  - Generación de binario nativo Linux ARM64 (`aarch64-linux-gnu`) probado para Raspberry Pi 3B/4/5 y Oracle Cloud ARM.
  - Generación de binario nativo Linux x86_64 (`x86_64-linux-gnu`) sin dependencias de librerías multilib i386.
  - Mantenimiento del binario actual i686 (`linux-x86`) para máxima compatibilidad con equipos antiguos.
  - Compatibilidad estricta con Netcode v38 (mismo hash, tickrate de 30Hz, desalineación cero en structs de red).
  - Publicación multi-arquitectura en GitHub Actions CI (`docker buildx` para `linux/amd64` y `linux/arm64`).
- Fuera:
  - Puertos gráficos OpenGL de 64 bits para clientes de escritorio (este spec cubre exclusivamente el servidor dedicado headless).
  - Sistemas de 16 bits o arquitecturas no-ARM/x86 (MIPS, RISC-V).

## Requisitos funcionales
- FR-1: El servidor debe compilar y enlazar como ejecutable nativo ELF AArch64 (`aarch64-linux-gnu`) sin warnings fatales | criterio: `file build/linux-arm64/halo` reporta `ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64`.
- FR-2: El servidor debe arrancar en modo headless (`null_renderer = true`) en un host ARM64 (o QEMU aarch64) y escuchar correctamente en el puerto UDP 2302 y HTTP 8080 | criterio: Respuesta HTTP 200 en `/api/settings` y socket UDP 2302 en estado listening.
- FR-3: El layout de memoria de las estructuras del juego y de los paquetes de red Netcode v38 en ARM64 y x86_64 debe ser idéntico al de i686 | criterio: Ninguna discrepancia de alineación en structs de red y tags (`assert(sizeof(...) == ...)`); los clientes oficiales v38 se conectan sin errores de protocolo.
- FR-4: El pipeline de CI en GitHub Actions debe compilar y empaquetar los 3 binarios (`halo-server-linux-x86`, `halo-server-linux-x64`, `halo-server-linux-arm64`) en cada release | criterio: Los artefactos existen en el workflow de GitHub Actions.

## Requisitos no funcionales
- NFR-1: Consumo de memoria en reposo en ARM64 < 120 MB de RAM | medicion: RSS reportado por `ps` en host o contenedor.
- NFR-2: Cero secretos o tokens en scripts de build o configuración del repositorio | verificacion: `git log` y `grep` sin strings sensibles.
- NFR-3: Binario headless sin dependencias externas pesadas | verificacion: `ldd` no requiere X11, Wayland, PulseAudio o PipeWire.

## Supuestos
- La Raspberry Pi 3B corre un sistema operativo de 64 bits (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit basado en Debian Bookworm/Bullseye o Ubuntu Server 64-bit).
- Clang y LLD soportan cross-compilation a `--target=aarch64-linux-gnu` en el entorno de compilación.

## Preguntas abiertas
- Ninguna bloqueante en este momento.

```

`specs/server-full-suite/plan.md`:

```md
# Architecture Plan: Halo Dedicated Server Complete Suite

## Arquitectura Modular

```
                           [ Motor Dedicated Server ]
                                      |
         +----------------------------+----------------------------+
         |                            |                            |
  [ xbox_files.c ]             [ server_web.c ]             [ server_webhooks.c ]
  - HALO_LOG_DIR               - /metrics (Prometheus)      - Discord Webhook
  - paths.logs                 - /api/login (Argon2id)      - Telegram Bot API
  - Rotacion a 64 MB           - RBAC (Owner/Admin/Mod)     - Eventos: Match, Carnage,
                               - Cookies HttpOnly / CSRF      Bans
```

## Decisiones de Arquitectura

### Decisión 1: Redirección de logs (`HALO_LOG_DIR`)
- **Contexto:** El motor original abre `d:\debug.txt` con la letra de unidad virtual `d:`.
- **Decisión:** Interceptar la resolución de la ruta `d:\debug.txt` en `xbox_files.c`. Si `config_string("paths.logs")` o la variable `HALO_LOG_DIR` existen, redirigir la apertura a ese directorio físico.
- **Alternativas descartadas:** Mapear enlaces simbólicos dentro del contenedor (frágil ante reinicios).

### Decisión 2: Autenticación Web y Sesiones
- **Contexto:** `app.js` ya soporta formulario de login y cookies de sesión si el backend devuelve roles y tokens CSRF.
- **Decisión:** Implementar autenticación basada en cookie `session_id` con SHA-256 HMAC / Argon2id en `server_web.c`. Si no hay contraseña configurada (`server.web_password = ""`), se mantiene el modo libre (`owner` automático) para conveniencia en redes locales.
- **Alternativas descartadas:** JWT sin estado (añade complejidad innecesaria en un servidor monoproceso en C).

### Decisión 3: Despachador de Webhooks asíncrono
- **Contexto:** Las llamadas HTTP externas a Discord o Telegram tardan entre 100 y 500 ms.
- **Decisión:** Despachar las peticiones en un hilo de trabajo en segundo plano mediante sockets TCP o libcurl/posix sockets, asegurando que el tickrate de 30 Hz del juego nunca sufra micro-tirones.

### Decisión 4: Formato del Exportador Prometheus (`/metrics`)
- **Contexto:** Administradores de infraestructura necesitan monitorizar servidores de juego mediante Grafana.
- **Decisión:** Generar las métricas directamente en memoria dentro del despachador HTTP (`server_web.c`) bajo la ruta `/metrics` con las métricas clave:
  `halo_server_uptime_seconds`, `halo_players_active`, `halo_players_max`, `halo_tickrate_hz`, `halo_match_seconds_remaining`.

```

`specs/server-full-suite/spec.md`:

```md
# Spec: Halo Dedicated Server Complete Suite (v1.3.0)

## Problema
El servidor dedicado de Halo CE se encuentra al 82% de completitud frente a servidores dedicados de nivel de producción modernos. Faltan cuatro módulos críticos requeridos por administradores, operadores de Unraid/Docker y comunidades:
1. Imposibilidad de redirigir los logs (`debug.txt`, `debug.old.txt`) a un directorio personalizado (`HALO_LOG_DIR`), obligando a usuarios de Unraid a exponer la raíz binaria.
2. Carencia de autenticación y control de acceso basado en roles (RBAC) con login web protegido por Argon2id y sesiones seguras en el Web Dashboard.
3. Carencia de integración nativa con Discord y Telegram mediante webhooks para notificar inicios de partida, resultados (carnage reports) y sanciones.
4. Ausencia de exportador de telemetría y métricas para observabilidad con Prometheus y Grafana (`/metrics`).

## Alcance
- Dentro:
  - **Módulo 1: Log Redirection (HALO_LOG_DIR / paths.logs):** Soporte en motor C para escribir y rotar logs en cualquier ruta configurada sin tocar la raíz de datos.
  - **Módulo 2: RBAC & Web Authentication:** Pasarela de login en el Web Dashboard (`/api/login`, `/api/logout`, `/api/session`), soporte de contraseña Argon2id, tokens CSRF, cookies de sesión y permisos jerárquicos (Owner, Admin, Moderator, Viewer).
  - **Módulo 3: Event Webhooks (Discord / Telegram):** Notificaciones HTTP asíncronas para eventos de servidor: arranque de mapa, ganador/marcador final y sanciones disciplinarias.
  - **Módulo 4: Observabilidad Prometheus (/metrics):** Endpoint `/metrics` con formato OpenMetrics estándar para monitoreo en tiempo real de jugadores, tickrate, ping y estado del servidor.
- Fuera:
  - Grabación de replays de cliente (requiere modificaciones en el renderizador de cliente fuera del alcance del servidor headless).
  - Modificación del protocolo de red de juego (Netcode v38 se mantiene 100% inalterado).

## Requisitos funcionales
- FR-1 [Logs]: Si `HALO_LOG_DIR` o `paths.logs` está definido, el motor crea el directorio y escribe `debug.txt` y `debug.old.txt` allí | criterio: El archivo se crea y escribe en la ruta especificada.
- FR-2 [RBAC]: Si `server.web_password` está configurado, la Web GUI oculta controles de administración hasta iniciar sesión | criterio: Peticiones no autorizadas a `/api/command`, `/api/settings` (PUT) y `/api/rotation` (PUT/POST) retornan HTTP 401.
- FR-3 [Webhooks]: Cuando una partida finaliza o un jugador es sancionado, el despachador de webhooks envía un payload JSON al webhook de Discord o Telegram configurado | criterio: Petición HTTP POST enviada con código de respuesta 200/204.
- FR-4 [Métricas]: `GET /metrics` expone métricas en formato texto Prometheus (players, tickrate, uptime, map_info) | criterio: `curl http://...:8080/metrics` devuelve cabeceras `# HELP` y `# TYPE` conformes a la especificación OpenMetrics.

## Requisitos no funcionales
- NFR-1: Cero secretos o webhooks en logs o repositorios | verificacion: Sanitización estricta en código y commits.
- NFR-2: La autenticación no debe añadir latencia al tick de juego de 30 Hz | medicion: Verificación de hash Argon2id ejecutada en el hilo web HTTP sin bloquear el bucle principal.
- NFR-3: Memoria en reposo del servidor debe mantenerse < 120 MB en ARM64 y x86 | medicion: RSS reportado por `ps`.

## Supuestos
- Los clientes se comunican exclusivamente por Netcode v38.
- La librería mbedtls ya enlazada en el proyecto provee primitivas criptográficas para hashing y tokens.

`specs/upstream-master-bridge/plan.md`:

```md
# Plan de Arquitectura: Integración con Master Server Oficial (v1.4.0)

## Aclaración sobre C vs Go
- **El Servidor de Juego Dedicado (OpenCE)**: Tanto en nuestra versión como en la oficial upstream, el servidor de juego **está 100% escrito en C** (`halo`). Maneja la física del motor de Halo CE original, mapas, colisiones, render nulo, red UDP y el servidor web HTTP embebido.
- **El Master Server Remoto (`opence-master-server`)**: Es un servicio de backend independiente que corre en la nube de OpenCE (`master.opencommunityedition.com`) escrito en **Go**. Actúa como directorio central/catálogo global. Los servidores dedicados en C se comunican con él vía peticiones HTTPS POST firmadas con Ed25519.

## Decisiones de Arquitectura

1. **Contexto**: Upstream introdujo `port/linux/src/server_master.c`, `server_mode.c` y `server_http.c`. Nuestra versión contiene un despachador HTTP optimizado (`server_web.c`) que añade `/metrics`, webhooks y persistencia `PUT /api/settings`.
2. **Decisión**: Integrar el despachador de publicación de `server_master.c` y la lógica de argumentos CLI (`--server`, `--keygen`, `--sign`) dentro de nuestra base de código, inyectando los endpoints comunitarios (`/metrics`, webhooks) en el servidor HTTP sin reemplazar los endpoints REST requeridos por `app.js`.
3. **Alternativas descartadas**:
   - Reemplazar completamente nuestro `server_web.c` por `server_http.c` de upstream: Descartado porque perderíamos el exportador `/metrics` de Prometheus, los webhooks y la adaptación para Raspberry Pi 3B.
   - Forzar a los clientes a usar listas no oficiales: Descartado porque aísla a la comunidad de los jugadores que usan clientes vanilla de OpenCE Build 289+.
4. **Consecuencias**:
   - Se mantiene la compatibilidad con ARM64 / x86_64.
   - El operador obtiene su clave de publisher ejecutando `./halo --keygen` y puede registrarla ante el bot oficial de OpenCE con `./halo --sign <nonce>`.

## Riesgos y Mitigación
- **Riesgo**: Que el Master Server oficial tarde en autorizar la clave vía Discord.
  - *Mitigación*: Mantener el modo híbrido (`_listing_dedicated` en brokers P2P) para que el servidor siga siendo descubrible de inmediato en el Server Browser mientras se completa la verificación manual.

```

`specs/upstream-master-bridge/spec.md`:

```md
# Upstream Master Server Bridge & Official Dedicated Architecture

## Problema
En OpenCE Build 289, el cliente del juego dejó de mostrar servidores dedicados en la pestaña oficial DEDICATED basándose en la bandera del host, exigiendo que provengan autenticados por un Master Server oficial (`master.opencommunityedition.com`) firmado mediante claves Ed25519 (`publisher.key`). Nuestro servidor opera actualmente en modo autónomo/P2P; aunque expone métricas Prometheus, Web Dashboard y webhooks, carece del subsistema que publica hacia el master server central de OpenCE con pruebas criptográficas (`--keygen`, `--sign`).

## Alcance
- Dentro:
  - Portar e integrar `server_master.c`, `server_mode.c` y soporte `--keygen`/`--sign`.
  - Habilitar autenticación con el master server oficial (`master.opencommunityedition.com`).
  - Preservar al 100% las funciones comunitarias exclusivas: Web Dashboard embebido, Prometheus `/metrics`, webhooks Discord/Telegram, selector Campaign/Multiplayer y soporte ARM64 (Raspberry Pi 3B).
  - Unificar el hilo HTTP entre las funciones nativas y nuestros endpoints enriquecidos.
- Fuera:
  - No se reemplaza el servidor dedicado del juego en Go: el binario del juego sigue siendo C nativo (`halo`). La implementación del master server upstream en Go (`opence-master-server`) se consume como servicio de catálogo remoto vía HTTPS.

## Requisitos funcionales
- FR-1: Generación y firma de clave de publisher mediante comandos CLI `./halo --keygen` y `./halo --sign <nonce>` | criterio: genera `publisher.key` (Ed25519) de 64 bytes y calcula firmas hex verificables.
- FR-2: Publicación periódica automática al Master Server oficial vía HTTPS cada 30 segundos | criterio: `server_master.c` despacha payloads JSON firmados a `https://master.opencommunityedition.com/publish` y procesa respuestas 200 OK.
- FR-3: Preservar endpoints comunitarios `/metrics`, `/api/rotation/play` y webhooks | criterio: un cliente curl a `/metrics` retorna telemetría Prometheus con el servidor en modo master server activo.
- FR-4: Registro de región (`server.region`) en el payload del master server | criterio: el master server recibe y publica la etiqueta `"region"` para que los clientes vean `EU`, `NA`, etc.

## Requisitos no funcionales
- NFR-1: Consumo de CPU < 2% en reposo durante el ciclo de publicación HTTPS | medición: top / pidstat en Linux x86_64 y ARM64.
- NFR-2: Cero fugas de claves privadas: `publisher.key` debe guardarse con permisos `0600` y nunca exponerse en logs ni respuestas web.

## Supuestos
- El Master Server oficial de OpenCE acepta solicitudes de operadores vía su bot de Discord con el comando `/apply`.
- El puerto UDP 2302 del servidor debe ser accesible desde internet para que la sonda de reachability del master server responda con éxito.

## Preguntas abiertas
- Ninguna. Protocolo y vectores criptográficos documentados en `docs/master_protocol.md`.

```

`systemd/halo-server.service`:

```service
[Unit]
Description=Halo: Combat Evolved dedicated server
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=halo
Group=halo
WorkingDirectory=/srv/halo
Environment=HALO_DATA_ROOT=/srv/halo
Environment=HOME=/srv/halo/home
# sin pantalla ni tarjeta de sonido: los drivers dummy de SDL
Environment=SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy
Environment=SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy
ExecStart=/srv/halo/halo
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateTmp=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

```
